Confirm both numbers with the Auditor before you set a closing date. State law assigns the bill to the grantor, meaning the seller (R.C. 319.202(D)).

  • Make the check payable to the Holmes County Auditor and send recording fees separately.
  • The office returns no change on an overpaid check and will not accept a signed blank check.
  • A check stopped on a transfer is referred to the county Prosecutor.
  • Attach form DTE 100, or DTE 100EX when the transfer qualifies for an exemption. Homestead property adds DTE 101 and current agricultural use land adds DTE 102.

Moving a mobile home title takes one more stamp. The Auditor will not process that transfer until the Treasurer's stamp shows the home's taxes are paid.

Recording charges and page layout

Most documents cost $34.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 per page after that, under R.C. 317.32 and 317.36. Senate Bill 94 amended the statute effective October 24, 2024, so a county may now add a preservation surcharge of as much as five dollars. Phone the office for the total on your page count.

Formatting can raise the bill. R.C. 317.114 sets the layout, and a paper that misses it is still recorded, for an extra $10.00 service charge plus a $10.00 housing trust fund charge. Before you print the deed, check these points:

  • type of 10 points or larger, in black or blue ink, with no highlighting
  • sheets between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches
  • a one inch margin at each side and the foot of every page
  • three blank inches at the head of page one, and an inch and a half on later pages

Court and taxing-authority papers, plats, DD-214s and state or federal documents are exempt.

Searching records and e-recording

Two search tools sit on the Recorder's page. AVA needs no login and fits a one-time lookup. Laredo Anywhere is for people who search often, and the county posts a setup guide in its document library. Both show images of deeds, easements, rights-of-way and leases. Other record types can be viewed from 1980 forward, and plats live on the Tax Map Department website.

The office accepts documents electronically, including deeds. It works with four vendors: ePN, Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services and CSC, which serve title companies, law firms and banks that record regularly. Most sellers never use this route directly, since the title company handles it at closing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Holmes County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Property Fraud Alert

Owners can sign up for Property Fraud Alert through the Recorder, and a flyer sits in the Recorder section of the county document library. An alert matters most to an owner who lives away from the house or who has just inherited it, because a forged deed or an unexpected lien only shows up in the public record after it is filed.

Once a sale closes, the recorded deed is the buyer's proof of ownership. Check that it shows the correct parcel, the Tax Map Office stamp and the Auditor's endorsement before anything is handed over.

Holmes County housing figures

Holmes County had 44,970 residents in July 2025 and 14,592 housing units. Owners occupy 79.0% of homes, the middle owner-occupied home is worth $267,700 and median household income is $76,140. Calling or visiting Suites 101, 102 and 107 often beats an online form here, and the county's heavy Amish population makes farm and acreage sales a common part of the market.

Military discharges and a seller's checklist

Soldier's discharges are filed here, but they stay out of the public record for 75 years. Only authorized parties, such as the discharged service member, a county service officer or an heir of a deceased service member, can obtain one. Anyone else sees just name, rank, birth date, discharge date and type.

Here is a short checklist before you sell: get the legal description reviewed by the Tax Map Office, collect the Planning Commission stamp if it applies, pay the Auditor's fees with the right DTE form, then record. If a mortgage is being paid off, ask the lender when the release will be filed. If you plan to mail the packet instead of walking it between suites, call each office first and confirm the fee it will want, then enclose a separate check and envelope for each stop. Keep copies of every stamped page, since they show the order in which the offices handled the deed if a question comes up later.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Can I pay the Holmes County Recorder by credit card?

Yes. The office accepts cash, check and credit card, and the same applies to deeds and other conveyance documents.

Is Tax Map approval needed before a Holmes County deed is recorded?

Yes, whenever the paper carries a legal description. The standards route all descriptions, land contracts, mineral deeds and easements to the Tax Map Office first, with a 24-hour review.

Who owes the conveyance fee on a Holmes County sale?

The seller owes it. R.C. 319.202(D) charges the grantor, and the Auditor's schedule prints $4.00 per thousand dollars of price plus $0.50 per parcel. Verify the figures with the Auditor.

Can a Holmes County deed go through the mail?

Yes. Follow the four-stop sheet in order, and enclose forms, fees and a pre-addressed, correctly stamped envelope for each office.

Who can obtain a recorded military discharge in Holmes County?

Only authorized parties, such as the discharged service member, a county service officer or an heir of a deceased service member. A discharge stays out of the public record for 75 years.

Where to take a deed in Norwalk

Take it to the Huron County Recorder at 12 E. Main Street, Suite 100, Norwalk, OH 44857. The office keeps weekday hours of 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM. Its phone is 419-668-1916, its fax is 419-663-4052, and document requests go to Recorder@huroncounty-oh.gov.

The real cutoff is 4:20 PM. Anything submitted later is recorded the next business day. Ohio recorders file instruments in the order they arrive and note the exact time (R.C. 317.13), so two deeds for the same house are ranked by that clock.

Electronic indexes and images of everything recorded since January 1, 1980 are meant to be posted online. A county may require a username and password but cannot charge for one. Copies still come from the Norwalk office.

Recording charges

The Recorder's fee table took effect January 1, 2025. Two pages cost $39.00, up from $34.00, because Senate Bill 94 created a $5.00 document preservation surcharge and Huron County started collecting it on the first day of that year.

Recording fee by page count (partial list)
PagesRecording fee
1 to 2$39.00
3$47.00
5$63.00
7$79.00
10$103.00

Past page two the price climbs $8.00 a page. Each marginal reference adds $4.00, and the standardization guidelines still apply. A mortgage release that points back to a recorded mortgage is the common reason for a marginal reference.

Recording a Huron County deed online

Nearly everything can be sent electronically. Plats and vacation documents are the exceptions and must be mailed or brought to Norwalk. Six submitting vendors are listed:

  • Corporation Service Company (CSC)
  • eRecording Partners Network (EPN)
  • Indecomm Global Services
  • Simplifile
  • Hopdox
  • File And Go

Each vendor sets its own pricing and onboarding, so contact one directly. The office also runs AlertMe, which sends a notice when a paper carrying a name you register is recorded or corrected. An owner who fears a forged filing against the family home can watch for it that way. The Public Access site searches recorded documents, and the Recorder asks that copy requests come by email or phone.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Huron County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What a deed must show before the Auditor transfers it

Chapter 14 of the county's conveyance standards, written jointly by the Auditor and the Engineer, lists what the deed has to carry. The Tax Map Department takes files first come, first served, and splits, combinations, annexations and subdivisions can run several days.

  • the grantor's original signature, or a certified copy of a court order
  • the volume and page of the last recorded deed in the chain of title
  • the grantee's full tax mailing address
  • the full names of grantor and grantee
  • the Auditor's parcel number and the site address
  • a completed DTE 100, or the exemption form when the transfer is exempt

The standards suggest a pre-transfer check at the Tax Map Department before anyone signs. The Auditor is at 12 E. Main Street, Suite 300, phone (419) 668-4304, on weekday hours that match the Recorder's.

The DTE 100 statement of value

This form travels with the deed. It breaks the price into a new mortgage, any balance assumed and cash, then subtracts whatever was paid for items other than real property. The conveyance fee is figured on the remainder.

Two questions affect the buyer's tax bill. One asks whether the home receives the senior, disabled or surviving spouse homestead exemption, which brings in form DTE 101. The other asks about current agricultural use valuation and form DTE 102. A final item is the owner-occupancy application for the 2.5% reduction on qualified levies, and the form warns that skipping it blocks the reduction until a new proper and timely application is filed.

The Auditor's receipt on the form covers the fee under R.C. 319.54(G)(3) and, where one exists, the Chapter 322 fee. Ask the Auditor what rate is in force.

Auditor forms around a home sale

Besides the conveyance forms, the Auditor's Forms page carries the tax applications a seller or buyer may need around closing. Several concern relief that either helps the seller or has to be reapplied for by the buyer:

  • DTE 105A and 105B, the homestead exemption applications for senior citizens, disabled persons and surviving spouses
  • DTE 105I, the homestead application for disabled service members and surviving spouses
  • DTE 105C, the 2.5% reduction on an owner-occupied home
  • DTE 26, the valuation deduction for damaged or destroyed real property
  • DTE 23A, the remission of late-payment penalties
  • DTE 1, the complaint against the valuation of real property

Your homestead status is disclosed on the DTE 100, and the buyer should file the owner-occupancy application when the house will be a principal residence. The Auditor's home page keeps a link to current homestead information.

Signing and recording the deed

The grantor signs, and under R.C. 5301.01 the signature is acknowledged before a judge or court clerk, a county auditor, a county engineer, a notary or a mayor. Most sellers use the notary at a title company or bank.

Recording follows. R.C. 5301.25 treats an unrecorded deed as fraudulent against a later buyer who paid without knowing of it, which is why closing agents file the same day.

The Recorder may decline a paper that is not required or authorized to be recorded, or that looks materially false or fraudulent. Someone refused can ask the Huron County Court of Common Pleas for an order. The Recorder has no duty to inspect a deed for mistakes, so the preparer must check the legal description, each name and the notary block. A deed returned for a defect loses its place in line.

Huron County housing at a glance

Huron County had 58,250 residents in July 2025 and 25,763 housing units, with 74.0% of homes owner-occupied. The middle owner-occupied home is valued at $166,000, median gross rent is $848 and median household income is $67,878.

Putting the steps in order

A typical Huron County sale runs like this. Ask the Tax Map Department to check the description before anyone signs. The seller signs before a notary, and the deed goes to the Auditor with a completed DTE 100 and the conveyance fee. After that the deed is recorded, ideally before 4:20 PM, either at the Norwalk counter or through one of the listed e-recording vendors. Keep the receipts from both offices with your closing file, and note the time stamp on the recorded deed. If the deed comes back for a defect, fix it and resubmit early in the day, because a returned deed loses its place in line.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

How much does the Huron County Recorder charge for a three-page deed?

$47.00 under the table effective January 1, 2025. Pages one and two total $39.00, the third adds $8.00, and a $4.00 charge applies to each marginal reference.

When does a Huron County deed miss same-day recording?

After 4:20 PM. Later submissions are recorded the next business day, though the office stays open until 4:30 PM on weekdays.

Can I view recorded Huron County documents from home?

The Public Access site searches the records, but copies come from the office. Email Recorder@huroncounty-oh.gov or call 419-668-1916.

Do plats go through e-recording in Huron County?

No. Plats and vacation documents are the two types left out of electronic recording and must be mailed or delivered to the Norwalk office.

Who approves a legal description in Huron County?

The County Auditor and the County Engineer, under R.C. 315.251 and 319.203. They may reject a nonconforming description and are expected to work out technical problems informally with the presenter.

Where to file a deed in Jackson County

Go upstairs to the third floor. The Recorder sits inside the courthouse at 226 East Main Street, Jackson, OH 45640, phone (740) 286-1919, fax (740) 286-8835. Counter service runs weekdays from 8:30 am to 4:00 pm, with a midday closure from 11:30 am to 12:30 pm. Time your visit around that hour.

You can pay with cash, a check or a debit or credit card. Cards add a $2.00 service fee. The county's official records begin in 1997. Anything older must be viewed and printed at the office, while later records are searchable online after you set up an account.

Recorder fees

Deeds, mortgages, leases, affidavits and most other recordable papers are priced the same way: $39.00 covers two pages, then $8.00 for each additional page. Each printed side counts as a page. The state fixes the price. One half is the recording fee itself, and the other half is sent to the Ohio Housing Trust Fund.

Jackson County Recorder fees
Paper or serviceFee
Deed, mortgage or lease (first two pages)$39.00
Each page past two$8.00
Marginal note on a release, assignment or amendment$4.00 each
Plat or condominium drawing, each 8 by 14 sheet$40.00
UCC filing against real estate$12.00 plus $4.00 per name indexed
Uncertified copy$2.00 a page
Certified copy$2.00 a page plus $1.00 for the seal

A veteran's service discharge and one certified copy carry no fee, and a zoning resolution costs $50.00.

What the Auditor adds before recording

The Auditor's transfers page lists two charges. The conveyance fee is $4.00 per thousand, and the transfer fee is fifty cents on each parcel. The conveyance rate was raised from $1.00 per thousand of the purchase price on March 24, 1993.

The Auditor is down the hall in the same courthouse, 226 East Main Street, Suite 5, phone (740) 286-4231, open 8:00 am to 4:00 pm. Under the Auditor's Tools menu you will find a Conveyance Calculator and a Sales Reports page. R.C. 319.202(D) puts the bill on the grantor, so you carry it as the seller. Forms on the site include:

  • DTE 100, the statement of value and fee receipt in one
  • DTE 100EX, the reason an exemption applies
  • DTE 100M and 100MEX, the manufactured and mobile home versions

Sequence matters: Auditor first, Recorder second. Changing who is named on title, whether adding a person or taking one off, needs a brand new deed, which clears the Auditor before it is recorded.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Jackson County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What happens if a deed is never recorded

Skip the recorder and a second buyer could end up owning your house. Under R.C. 5301.25 the deed has to be recorded where the land lies. Until it is, the law treats it as fraudulent toward any later purchaser who paid in good faith.

A few things sellers often ask the Recorder:

  • Nearly every record is open to the public. Military service records go only to the veteran who earned them, with proof of ID.
  • A will is recorded through Probate Court, which charges $46.00.
  • The office suggests an attorney or other professional draft your deed.

A name error means a fresh deed, and you start again at the Auditor.

Ordering copies and searching records

Viewing most records online starts with an account. A deed from the 1980s predates the 1997 start of the official records and has to be pulled at the courthouse itself.

To order an image, email the document's book and page to recordersoffice@jacksoncounty.us. Copies run $2.00 a page, payable by cash or check. Someone planning to list a house can also open the Sales Reports page on the Auditor's site, next to the Conveyance Calculator and a Tax Estimator.

Other papers the Recorder files

The county's fee list reaches well past deeds. Watch for these when a title search digs up old liens or a prior owner left paperwork behind:

  • federal tax liens and other federal liens: $5.00
  • releases or partial releases of those liens: $3.00
  • a living will or health care power of attorney: $40.00
  • zoning amendments: $20.00
  • no fee for personal property tax, workers' compensation, recognizance and unemployment compensation liens, or for certificates of premium due

R.C. 317.32 and 317.36 back these charges. When an old lien turns up on your parcel, ask the Recorder which release clears it and what it costs. A release is its own filing and is not folded into the deed.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Jackson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Contesting a valuation after buying

Disputes about value go to the county Board of Revision. Its members are the Auditor, the Treasurer and the President of the County Commissioners, or their designees. The board adjusts values, not tax dollars. Submit form DTE 1 to the Auditor, who serves as secretary to the board, by March 31.

Watch the details. The form needs your own opinion of value on line 8 and a notary's stamp. You generally get one complaint per three-year period, and withdrawing one still uses it up. Proof is your job, and the result can go up, go down or stay put. It will not weigh a percentage jump in the tax bill or a neighbor's lower valuation.

Questions about paying a bill go to the County Treasurer at 740-286-2402. You can pay real estate taxes online or on the Autoagent phone line, 1-844-674-1100, and skip the trip to the courthouse.

Jackson County housing figures

Jackson County counted 32,817 residents in July 2025 and 14,665 housing units. Owners live in 73.9% of homes. A median owner-occupied home is worth $150,700, and median household income is $57,106. The Auditor's site counts 28,916 parcels for 2024.

Steps for a seller

Have the deed drafted, preferably by an attorney. Sign it, then take it to Suite 5 to pay the conveyance and transfer fees, with form DTE 100 or the exemption form. Carry the stamped deed up to the third floor and pay the recording fee, mindful of the lunch closure. Request a copy for your files. The buyer's title company usually handles most of this at closing, so confirm who is carrying the deed to each office and by what day, and keep your receipts from both counters until the sale is fully recorded. A mortgage payoff produces a release that is recorded separately, with its own page charge and perhaps a marginal notation. Have your title company confirm it was filed. After closing, the buyer can search the new deed online, assuming it was recorded after 1997 and the buyer has set up an account. Should the recorded paper contain a mistake, call the Recorder right away.

Frequently asked questions

How much does the Jackson County Recorder charge for a three-page deed?

$47.00. That is the $39.00 two-page price plus $8.00 for page three. A marginal note adds $4.00 apiece, so find out whether your paper needs any.

Is the Jackson County Recorder open over lunch?

No. It closes from 11:30 am to 12:30 pm and otherwise serves the public weekdays between 8:30 am and 4:00 pm.

What conveyance fee does Jackson County charge?

The rate is $4.00 for every thousand dollars of purchase price, with $0.50 more per parcel as a transfer fee. The $4.00 figure has applied since March 24, 1993.

Does paying the Jackson County Recorder by card cost extra?

Yes, by $2.00. That service fee applies to debit and credit cards only, not to cash or checks.

Does the Jackson County Recorder record wills?

No. A will is recorded in Probate Court, at a cost of $46.00. The Recorder files deeds, mortgages and similar land records.

The Recorder's office in Steubenville

Think of this office as the county's memory for land: every deed, mortgage and other charge on a Jefferson County parcel ends up in its permanent record. The office is at 301 Market Street, Steubenville, OH 43952, and keeps weekday hours of 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. Request the current fee schedule when you phone. The staff is small, so send complete packets and call ahead.

All land in the county is recorded in this one place, from lots in Steubenville and Toronto to farms in the townships. Property across the river in Brooke or Hancock County, West Virginia, falls under West Virginia's own recording system.

What goes into a recording fee

R.C. 317.32 sets each recording charge as two equal halves: a base fee for the recorder and a matching fee for the Ohio housing trust fund. Get the Recorder's total for your paper before you write a check.

Statutory recording charges, each paid twice (recorder and trust fund)
ServiceEach of the two fees
Pages one and twoSeventeen dollars
Each added legal-size page or partial pageFour dollars
Marginal reference made by separate instrumentTwo dollars
Certified copy, per pageOne dollar, plus fifty cents for the seal

Senate Bill 94, effective October 24, 2024, let counties tack on a preservation surcharge of up to five dollars, kept in the general fund. Whether Jefferson County does so, and for how much, is a question for the Recorder.

Conveyance charges a seller pays

The Auditor's counter collects in two layers. First comes the Auditor's fee under R.C. 319.54(G)(3): ten cents per hundred dollars of value, fractions counted, with a one dollar floor. On top of that, R.C. 322.02 lets a county adopt a transfer tax, capped at thirty cents per hundred dollars.

The county's 2025 annual financial report refers to a four mill permissive conveyance fee, with one of those mills dedicated to the GIS Fund by the commissioners. The Auditor is at 301 Market Street, P.O. Box 159, Steubenville, with phone (740) 283-8511 and fax (740) 283-8520. Call that office to confirm the rate, since a permissive levy is set by commissioner resolution.

Under R.C. 319.202(D) the seller pays. A transfer that qualifies as exempt carries a written statement of the reason in place of the fee.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Jefferson County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Family transfers that skip the conveyance fee

The statute lists about two dozen exemptions. These are the ones families use most:

  • a gift from one spouse to the other, or from a parent to a child or the child's spouse
  • a deed passing between heirs or devisees of one decedent, as long as no money is paid
  • a deed placing the house in a trust the maker can cancel at will
  • a corrective or confirming deed that repairs one already of record
  • an interest worth one hundred dollars or less
  • a court-ordered transfer, unless it follows a sale under that order

Selling to an outside buyer is different. Even a quick as-is cash sale is a fee-paying transfer.

Order of steps: Auditor, then Recorder

The Auditor is first in line. If the county levies a transfer tax, the grantor owes it, paid to the auditor when the deed is delivered and before it is shown to the recorder (R.C. 322.02). The Auditor notes the fee amount on the deed, and the deed then goes to the Recorder.

A Steubenville title company can file a closing package electronically instead of carrying it across the floor, since Ohio recorders, auditors and engineers must provide electronic recording of conveyance papers (R.C. 317.13). If you are handling the deed yourself, carry the signed, notarized original in case the office wants paper.

What the Recorder does with your deed

Once the deed arrives with the Auditor's mark on it, the Recorder checks that it can be filed, enters it in the permanent record and returns it. After that the public record names the owner of the parcel. Before it, a buyer's claim is weaker than it looks, so closing agents do not let a signed deed sit on a desk.

The same counter handles the other papers that tie to your parcel. The buyer's new mortgage is recorded here, and so is the release that clears your old loan. Easements and leases go through the same office. A stray lien or an old mortgage nobody ever released can slow a closing by days, so raise it with your title company before you list.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Jefferson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling for cash in Jefferson County

A cash buyer has no lender's appraisal or underwriting to wait on, so the courthouse side is a short chain: deed, Auditor, Recorder. The fees stay the same, though. Recording charges and the conveyance fee come due on a cash sale just as on a financed one, and you pay the conveyance fee at closing.

A house that needs work or has an unpaid tax bill calls for an early payoff figure from the title company. Amounts owed on the parcel come out of your proceeds, and the title company cannot promise a closing date without them. Heirs selling an inherited house should read the exemption list above first, since a deed between heirs with no money changing hands may owe nothing.

Housing figures for Jefferson County

Jefferson County had 63,597 residents and 30,964 housing units in 2025, and owners occupy 70.5% of homes. The typical owner-occupied home sells near a $127,800 value, monthly gross rent is $835 and household income is $59,055. The county's population has slid 2.5% since the 2020 base, so expect a buyer pool that leans local. Many residents work in the Weirton-Steubenville metropolitan area, which adds Brooke and Hancock counties in West Virginia. Buyers who commute across the river may be shopping in both states, so be ready to explain Ohio's process if an out-of-state agent calls. Pricing near the river towns often moves with job news from the Steubenville area, and a clean deed with clear paperwork keeps a sale on schedule when a buyer is on a deadline.

Before you take the deed in

Pull these together first: the signed, notarized deed, the parcel number and the full legal description. Phone the Auditor about the conveyance fee and the permissive fee. Phone the Recorder for the total on your page count, including any preservation surcharge. An exempt transfer needs its exemption statement stapled to the deed.

Which office records the deed on a house in Steubenville?

The Jefferson County Recorder at 301 Market Street. Steubenville is inside Jefferson County, so deeds there are filed in that office.

Does Jefferson County charge the optional document preservation surcharge?

Ask the Recorder. State law lets a county add up to five dollars, and the office can say what, if anything, it adds to a deed.

Who pays the conveyance fee on a Jefferson County sale?

The seller does. As grantor, you owe the Auditor's fee and any Chapter 322 transfer tax the county levies (R.C. 319.202(D)).

Does a gift of a house from a parent to a child owe the conveyance fee?

No, subdivision (d) of R.C. 319.54(G)(3) exempts it. The deed still goes to the Auditor with an exemption statement before it is recorded.

What is the four mill fee in the Jefferson County financial report?

It is the county's permissive conveyance fee. The commissioners dedicated one mill of it to the county's GIS Fund, which keeps the parcel maps current.

Where a Knox County seller records a deed

The recorder in Mount Vernon files Knox County deeds, but the auditor sees them first. The auditor's office is at 117 East High Street, Suite 120, Mount Vernon, OH 43050. Weekday hours are 8:00 to 4:00, the real estate desk answers at 740-393-6745, and the exemption desk at 740-393-6748. Phone the recorder's office for counter hours, payment methods and mailing rules before a deed goes in the mail.

Ohio gives each county a single recorder. Whether the house sits in town, near Fredericktown or around Gambier, the paperwork follows the same route through that one Mount Vernon office.

What the auditor charges when a deed transfers

Knox County's conveyance fee is $3.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price. Section 319.54(G)(2) adds fifty cents per transfer or entry. After the auditor, the recorder bills under section 317.32, where each charge pairs a base fee with a housing trust fund fee.

What a Knox County deed can cost
ChargeAmount
Conveyance fee (auditor)$3.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price
Transfer or entry (auditor)$0.50 each
Recording a two page deed$17 base fee, matched by a $17 housing trust fund fee
Every page past two$4 base fee, matched by a $4 housing trust fund fee
Preservation surchargeUp to $5, a county option
Marginal reference$2 plus $2 for each reference
Deed that ignores the layout rules$10 plus $10 on top of the usual charge

Ask the recorder whether the surcharge applies and what your page count totals.

The statement of value: who files and who pays

The buyer files it, and the seller pays, under section 319.202. The figure reported is the full price, mortgage included, and a false number is a violation. A county transfer tax, if one is levied, is collected the same way before the deed moves on to the recorder.

Knox County's auditor posts these forms for a sale:

  • DTE 100 records the statement of value and doubles as the receipt.
  • DTE 100(EX) names the reason a deed owes nothing.
  • DTE 101 discloses a conveyance of homestead property.
  • DTE 102 covers land enrolled in the current agricultural use valuation, common on farm acreage here.

The statute asks the buyer to affirm that the seller was questioned about any homestead reduction and any farm valuation. Tell the closing agent about either one early.

If your land is in current agricultural use valuation and the buyer plans to change how it is used, the change can trigger a recoupment charge, so raise that with the auditor before you set a closing date.

Deeds that owe no conveyance fee

The exemption list in section 319.54(G)(3) is long. The entries a homeowner is likeliest to use:

  • Gifts between spouses, or from a parent to a child.
  • Transfers among a decedent's heirs when no money changes hands.
  • Deeds into a trust the maker can revoke, and deeds back out of it.
  • Corrective deeds that repair an earlier recorded one.
  • Interests worth $100 or less.

Government, charity and court-ordered transfers appear on the list too. An exempt deed still needs the exemption form, so ask the real estate desk which form fits.

How a deed must be laid out

Section 317.114 asks for ten point type or larger, paper between letter and legal size, dark ink, no highlighter, one inch margins on the sides and bottom, and a three inch clear band across the top of page one. The recorder will still take a deed that misses these, at the added cost shown in the table. Court filings, plats, agency papers and instruments signed before July 1, 2009 are outside the rule.

A step by step route for a Knox County sale

Start with the legal description and parcel number, and compare them with the auditor's parcel search. Have the deed prepared by a closing agent or attorney and signed. Take it to the auditor at Suite 120 with the right DTE form and pay the conveyance fee and the transfer fee. The deed then goes to the recorder in Mount Vernon, which charges its own base and housing trust fund fees by page count.

Before any of that, call both offices. The auditor can say which form fits your transfer, and the recorder can say whether the preservation surcharge applies and how payment is taken. A deed that follows the layout rules avoids the extra $10 plus $10 charge, so check the margins, ink and type size before it is signed.

If the parcel is part of a larger tract, ask the auditor early whether a split must be approved first. A division of valuation on split acreage is its own form, and the recorded deed should match the new parcel description.

Knox County housing figures

Knox County had 64,002 people in mid 2025, a gain of 2.0 percent since April 2020, living in 26,668 housing units. Three out of four homes are owner occupied (75.5 percent). The median home value is $239,400 and median gross rent is $950. The county's 23,491 households have a median income of $73,878, and farmland covers a large share of the land, so acreage sales are common.

What to check on the auditor's site before listing

The auditor runs a real estate search portal that works on phones and tablets, plus a tax estimator, a GIS and tax map page and a downloadable property data correction form. If a deed splits acreage, the forms page carries a split form and a form for the proposed division of valuation on split acreage, which matters for owners selling off a lot from a larger farm parcel.

  • Run the parcel search and compare the owner name and acreage with your deed.
  • Try the tax estimator for a rough tax figure to show a buyer.
  • Download the property data correction form if a record shows the wrong square footage or building count.
  • Read the sheriff sales page if the parcel has a case in court.

Property owners' phone numbers are kept private, so buyers and agents should contact you through the listing.

Tax due dates and disputes

Call the Knox County Treasurer for the next pair of due dates. The auditor links to the treasurer's payment site from its home page.

Value complaints go to the Knox County Board of Revision. The board organizes on January 4, 2027 and takes formal complaints from January 1 through March 31, 2027, and the 2026 returns can be inspected at the auditor's office. The auditor's menu also links pages for the owner occupancy reduction, homestead exemption, CAUV soil rates, agricultural districts and sheriff sales.

When a tax bill is still open at closing, the title company typically gets a payoff from the treasurer and settles it from the proceeds. Request that figure as soon as a contract exists. Keep your own copy of the payoff letter and the settlement statement.

Who records a deed in Knox County, Ohio?

The Knox County Recorder in Mount Vernon. The deed visits the auditor at 117 East High Street, Suite 120 beforehand. Call the recorder for current hours and mailing instructions.

What is the Knox County conveyance fee?

The county charges $3.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price, and section 319.54(G)(2) adds fifty cents per transfer or entry. Under section 319.202 the seller bears it.

What if my deed ignores the margin and ink rules?

The recorder takes it anyway and collects an extra $10 base fee and $10 housing trust fund fee. Court papers, plats, agency documents and instruments from before July 1, 2009 are excluded.

Can I give a Knox County house to my child without the conveyance fee?

A gift from a parent to a child is on the exemption list in section 319.54(G)(3). File the DTE 100(EX) with the auditor. The recorder's own charges still apply.

Which forms apply to farm ground or a homestead parcel in Knox County?

The auditor lists DTE 101 for homestead property and DTE 102 for current agricultural use valuation property. Ask the auditor about any recoupment charge on farm land before closing.

How a deed gets recorded in Lake County

It takes two counters in Painesville. The Transfer Office (the Auditor's first floor) comes first, where you complete an Exempt Form or a Conveyance Fee Form and get the deed stamped. The Recorder, on the lower level of the Administration Building, comes second and processes the deed on the spot.

The Recorder is at 105 Main Street, Lower Level, with P.O. Box 490, Painesville, OH 44077, phone (440) 350-2510 and email recorder@lakecountyohio.gov. Counter service runs weekdays from 8 a.m. until 4 p.m., closed on holidays, and the last recordings of the day should be in before 3:45.

A mailed filing has its own checklist. Each auditor and engineer stamp has to be on the deed already, and the envelope needs a cover letter, one check for the Recorder, one for the Auditor and a stamped return envelope. If the Auditor's stamp is missing, the deed comes back rejected.

Recorder and Auditor charges

The Recorder bills $34.00 for a two page deed and $5.00 for preservation, and each page past the second adds $8.00. The Auditor collects its own transfer charges, which is why the office wants two checks.

Lake County deed charges
ChargeAmountPayee

Each page after two$8.00Recorder

Conveyance fee$4.00 per $1,000 of valueAuditor
Transfer fee$0.50 for each parcelAuditor

The $4.00 breaks into a $1.00 state share and a $3.00 county share. The county piece was set by a commissioners' resolution dated March 26, 1990 under section 322.02.

Paperwork the Auditor wants with a transfer

Either side of the deal, or a representative, may hand in the deed, and mail is accepted. Everything must be complete, signed and notarized. The Transfer Office takes transfers between 8 and 4.

  • A DTE 100 or DTE 100EX goes with every transfer.
  • Parcels in the homestead or CAUV farm programs need a notarized DTE 101 or DTE 102 first.
  • A sale of anything short of a whole platted sublot, such as a piece of a sublot or a metes and bounds tract, must clear the Tax Map Department. Exempt transfers skip that stop.
  • Taking someone off a deed means drafting a new deed, so call a title company or attorney.

The county posts owner names exactly as the recorded deed spells them, so a typo on the deed travels into the tax records.

Transfers exempt from the conveyance fee

Section 319.54(G)(3) holds the exemption list, and the reason is written on the form that section 319.202 requires. Examples that fit house sales:

  • A deed given only as security for a debt, or releasing that security.
  • A sale for delinquent taxes or assessments.
  • Survivorship transfers under sections 5302.17 or 5302.18.
  • A deed to a trustee when the maker kept an unlimited power to revoke.
  • A transfer to a non-dealer who is only a stop on the way to a prompt resale.

One shortcut: a Transfer on Death Beneficiary Designation Affidavit skips the Auditor and goes straight to the Recorder, with the recording fee and a return envelope.

E-recording and record searches

A deed can be e-recorded through four partners: Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile and Hop Docs. You deal with one of those firms, because the Recorder's office does not operate the portal itself.

For research, the AVA search engine gives basic results and Laredo Select goes deeper, but it needs a registered account. Filings cannot carry watermarks. The office's services menu also lists a property fraud alert and a video chat on that topic.

The Recorder's guidelines restate section 317.114. A deed outside them is still accepted but costs the $20.00 penalty. Before signing, confirm:

  • Black or blue ink, with nothing highlighted.

  • A title, a date, typed names and titles under every signature, and a notary block that shows the commission expiration.
  • The preparer's name and a full legal description.

When one document refers to an earlier one, cite its number, or its book and page, along with the recording date. Each such reference adds $4.00.

Tax questions at a Lake County closing

Real estate taxes for 2026, payable in 2027, are due February 24 and July 21, 2027, and bills mail out in mid-January and mid-June. A buyer's lender or the title company will ask for the status of those halves, so request the Treasurer's payoff before the closing date. The Treasurer's billing line is (440) 350-2516, and the Auditor's real estate staff answer address and credit questions at (440) 350-2532.

If a record shows a wrong owner address, the Auditor corrects owner addresses while the Treasurer handles the tax mailing address, so changes may need two calls.

Putting your trip in order

Gather the signed, notarized deed and any exemption or value form before you leave home. Stop at the Transfer Office first, pay the conveyance and transfer fees and get the stamp. Walk the stamped deed down to the Recorder and pay its charges with a separate check. If the parcel is only part of a sublot, visit the Tax Map Department before the Auditor. Leave time before 3:45 so the deed is recorded the same day, and keep the receipts for your closing file. If your lender is paying off a mortgage, ask your title company to confirm that the release was filed, since it is a separate recording at the same counter. When money changes hands and the parcel is anything other than a full sublot in a platted subdivision. Part of a sublot and metes and bounds tracts both qualify. Exempt transfers do not need it.

Where the Lawrence County recorder's office is

The office is the county's permanent land file. Documents it handles every day include warranty and quit claim deeds, survivorship deeds, sheriff's deeds, certificates of transfer, affidavits of transfer, life estate terminations and transfer on death designation and confirmation affidavits. It also files mortgage releases and assignments, land contracts, plats, powers of attorney, zoning maps and a long run of liens, from mechanic's liens to federal tax liens and child support liens.

What it costs to record a deed

On January 1, 2025 most recording fees went up by $5.00, the preservation surcharge that Senate Bill 94 allowed. A one or two page document now runs $39.00 and every added page costs $8.00. Half of what the office collects is sent to the state for the Ohio Housing Trust Fund, consistent with section 317.32.

Lawrence County Recorder charges for a deed
ChargeAmount
One or two pages$39.00
Each added page$8.00
Ten pages in all$103.00

The recorder's fee is only one piece of closing. The credits on second half 2025 tax bills are another, and the auditor posts those by school district.

Avoiding the extra $20 charge

Prepare the deed to the layout in section 317.114, which covers documents prepared after June 30, 2009. A deed that misses it costs $20.00 more. The office's checklist:

  • Computer-printed type, 10 point or larger.
  • Paper no smaller than 8.5 by 11 and no larger than 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Black or blue ink, never highlighter.
  • A one inch margin down both sides and along the bottom of every page.
  • A 3 inch strip across the top of page one reserved for the recorder, auditor and engineer, then 1.5 inches on later pages.

Court and taxing authority papers, plats, DD214 discharges, state or federal documents and older instruments fall outside the rule. A margin guidelines PDF on the site helps whoever drafts the deed.

The auditor comes first

The auditor is at 111 S Fourth Street, phone (740) 533-4310, open weekdays 8 to 4. Section 319.202 sets the routine: the buyer files a statement of value, the seller pays the conveyance fee and the auditor endorses the deed.

The state charge in section 319.54(G)(3) is $1 or ten cents per $100, whichever is more, and a county can add a transfer tax capped at thirty cents per $100 under section 322.02. Totals differ by county, so the quickest check is the Conveyance Fee Calculator in the Tools menu of the auditor's site, which includes the parcel transfer fee. Type in a parcel count and a sale price, and it returns a charge.

Searching Lawrence County records

The current index runs from 1982 for deeds, 1988 for mortgages, 1989 for financing statements and 1981 for leases, liens and miscellaneous records. A second online index reaches much further back.

  • Deed grantor and grantee entries date from 1818 to 1984, and mortgages from 1834 to 1988.
  • Plats are listed from 1818 to 2010, and leases from 1864 to 1981.
  • Index books online include deed volumes 1 through 475 and mortgage volumes 82 through 441.

Staff can help you search during business hours. Older easements can hide before 1982, so ask where the older books begin for your parcel if a title search stops at the current deed index.

An Inflation Cap Credit appears on second half 2025 real estate bills. It is based on new revenue each school district gained from the 20 mill floor measured against inflation, and it did not alter any appraised value. A buyer or title agent can view the credit by searching the parcel on the auditor's site.

An owner who paid before the credit was applied needs to do nothing, because any overpayment rolls into the 2026 first half bill. Ask the auditor how a carried credit should show on a closing statement.

Tools on the auditor's site

Beyond the calculator, the Tools menu holds a Tax Estimator, a Sales Report, a Sales List and a Delinquency Report. The sales reports list recent sales in the county, which helps when you set a price. The site also carries a GIS parcel viewer through its map link, and a search page that shows the appraisal and payment history for any parcel.

A simple order of operations

Have the deed drafted to the layout rules and signed. Take it to the auditor, who collects the conveyance fee and endorses it, then to the recorder in Suite 21, which charges by page count. Before you do, run the calculator so the check is the right size. Mortgage releases and any older liens are recorded by the same office, so ask your title company to confirm each one was filed. Keep the endorsed deed and the receipt together for your closing file.

If your deed carries any reference to an earlier recorded document, count it before you leave home, since each reference adds $4.00 to the bill. Call the recorder at 740-533-4314 if you are unsure how many pages your signed deed runs, because the page count sets the fee. If the paper misses the margin rules the office still records it, but you pay the extra $20.00, so a quick check of type size and ink color saves money. Ironton sellers can also use the sales report on the auditor's site to see what nearby homes brought before settling on an asking price.

The recorder accepts it and adds $20.00. The 3 inch top margin on page one is reserved for the recorder, auditor and engineer. Court papers, plats, DD214s, state or federal documents and older instruments are exempt from the rule.

Where to record a Licking County deed

Deeds and mortgages for Licking County land go to the recorder's office at 20 S. Second Street in Newark, OH 43055. Call (740) 670-5300 with questions or send a fax to (740) 670-5303. The counter is open 8 AM to 4:30 PM on weekdays, and recording runs from 8:30 AM to 4:15 PM.

Staff examine each document, assign it a unique document number and a recording time, and use that time to fix the order of filings. Records reach back to the early 1800s. Anyone can search the paper index and record books at the counter for no charge, and staff will help with the search.

Online viewing covers documents recorded since September 22, 1997, including deeds, mortgages, releases, assignments and UCC statements. Anything older is a trip to the counter.

Recording fees

The county's own fee sheet uses a simple formula: number of pages times $8, plus $23. A marginal reference costs $4. A $5 preservation surcharge applies per document for standard document types. Ask the recorder how the surcharge shows up in your total before you write the check.

Licking County recording fees by document length
Document lengthRecording fee
1 to 2 pages$39.00
3 pages$47.00
4 pages$55.00
10 pages$103.00
20 pages$183.00
30 pages$263.00
Marginal reference$4.00

Other charges follow the Ohio Recorders' Association fee table. Photocopies and plat copies are $1.00 plus $1.00 per page. A certified copy is $1.00 plus $1.00 per page, with a seal fee of 50 cents plus 50 cents. A document that fails the state layout rules adds $10.00 plus $10.00.

Documents recorded around a house sale

The state fee table groups a long list of instrument types under the basic page charge. These are the ones most tied to a sale, a payoff or an inheritance:

  • Warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, survivorship deeds and limited warranty deeds.
  • Executor's, administrator's, guardian's, trustee's and sheriff's deeds.
  • Certificates of transfer and transfer on death designation affidavits.
  • Mortgages, assignments, modifications, satisfactions and releases of lien.
  • Affidavits on facts relating to title, affidavits of surviving spouse and affidavits of successor trustee.
  • Memoranda of trust, powers of attorney, land contracts and easements.
  • Mechanic's liens, lis pendens notices and Medicaid estate recovery liens and their releases.

Military discharges record without a fee. Federal tax liens carry their own listed charge of $5.00.

Stop at the auditor first

No deed skips the auditor. Under section 319.202, the grantee or an agent declares the value conveyed, and the auditor stamps the deed with the fee. An exempt transfer needs only a stated reason.

A conveyance, exempt transfer, split or merge has to arrive by 4 p.m. to clear that day. The auditor is at 20 South Second Street, (740) 670-5040.

The seller pays the state conveyance fee at the auditor's counter. A county real property transfer tax would be collected there too, but only if commissioners enacted one under section 322.02, at no more than 30 cents per $100. Ask the auditor whether one exists before you pick a closing date. If it does, payment comes before the trip to the recorder.

Searching and watching Licking County records

The recorder runs a PaxWorld public access site at apps.lickingcounty.gov. You create an account with a username and password. Images you buy download to your computer, so allow downloads in your browser.

The same site offers an AlertMe service that sends a notice when a document is recorded in your name. That is handy for owners who worry about fraudulent filings against their property.

Title companies, law firms and banks that file often can use eRecording. The county names four vendors:

  • CSC eRecording Solutions
  • ePN, the eRecording Partners Network
  • Indecomm Global Services
  • Simplifile

Electronic filing can cut turnaround from three to five working days down to minutes or hours, and recording fees are paid electronically.

Licking County housing market snapshot

Licking County had 73,930 housing units in July 2025 and 68,620 households across the 2020 to 2024 survey years. Owned homes are valued around $275,200, and about three in four are lived in by the owner. Rent averages $1,078, and a homeowner with a loan pays about $1,693 monthly. Population rose from 178,501 in April 2020 to an estimated 185,564 in July 2025.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Licking County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How a payoff or an inheritance shows up in the record

A sale usually produces more than one recorded paper. The buyer's deed goes on record, and the seller's old mortgage is cleared by a satisfaction or release that the lender files. The state sheet lists satisfaction, release, partial release and cancellation as separate document types. A marginal reference costs $4 when the recorder notes a link to an earlier filing.

Inherited property follows a different path. An executor's or administrator's deed, a certificate of transfer or a transfer on death designation affidavit can move title without a conventional sale, and each is recorded like any other deed. If the owner received Medicaid benefits, a Medicaid estate recovery lien and its release are recordable too. If one turns up in the chain of title, raise it with the title company before closing.

Searching old deeds and county lines

Licking County was carved out of Fairfield County in 1808, so the earliest history of a parcel may sit under the parent county's name. The recorder's holdings go back to the early 1800s, and staff will help a searcher read the index. Seven counties touch Licking County, so a parcel near a county line can carry a description that mentions Knox, Delaware, Franklin or another neighbor.

Acreage needs a wider look. Developers make frequent offers for farmland near New Albany. A deed search for a rural parcel should cover every transfer and any easements, and the state table lists agricultural easements and conservation easements as their own document types.

Order of steps on closing week

First the title company or attorney prepares the deed and the buyer and seller sign. Next the deed goes to the auditor for the conveyance statement and the fee. Then it moves to the recorder, who examines it, assigns the document number and sets the recording time. Last, the lender files its satisfaction for the seller's old mortgage. A seller who is not waiting on a lender payoff still needs the deed recorded before the buyer's ownership shows in the county index.

What to bring when you record in person

Bring the signed original, the fee for the page count, and proof that the auditor has already stamped the deed. Check that the document meets the state layout rules so the extra $10.00 plus $10.00 charge never applies. If you want a certified copy afterward, ask at the same visit.

Frequently asked questions

When is the Licking County recorder open?

Staff are in from 8 AM until 4:30 PM on weekdays, and recording itself happens between 8:30 AM and 4:15 PM. Call (740) 670-5300 before a holiday.

What would a two-page Licking County deed cost to record?

The county sheet lists $39.00 for one to two pages, based on pages times $8 plus $23. A third page brings the fee to $47.00.

Is searching Licking County records free?

Searching the index and record books at the recorder's counter is free. The online PaxWorld site requires an account, and purchased images download from the site.

Do I need the auditor before I record a Licking County deed?

Yes, the auditor endorses the deed and collects the conveyance fee first. For same-day processing the deed must reach the auditor by 4 p.m.

Can a title company e-record in Licking County?

Yes, the recorder accepts electronic filings through four listed eRecording vendors. Recorded documents come back electronically.

Recorder's office in Bellefontaine

The Logan County recorder sits in the annex at 100 S. Madriver Street, Bellefontaine, OH 43311. Call 937-599-7201. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 until 4:30, and Wednesday is the day it issues Veteran ID cards.

The recorder keeps the land ownership record and every lien against land. Each filing is stored in archival form and indexed so a searcher can trace ownership forward in time. Title examiners, attorneys, genealogists and historians all use those files.

The Logan Online portal has a Recorder's Document Search for looking up filed documents. The recorder also publishes Document Standardization Guidelines, a historical page and a Veteran ID Card Program page.

Filing fees

A short schedule appears on the county's recordable documents page. Everything the recorder collects goes into the county general fund. Phone 937-599-7201 for a total on a lengthy document.

Logan County recording fees
ChargeFee
First 2 pages$39
Each additional page$8
Non-standardization fee$20
Marginal reference, each$4

Layout rules that trigger the $20 fee

The extra $20 applies to paper that ignores Ohio Revised Code 317.114. The county's guidelines tie the rule to documents prepared after June 30, 2009, and spell out the specifications:

  • Type no smaller than 10 point.
  • Sheets between letter size and legal size, meaning 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Ink in black or blue, with no highlighter marks.
  • One inch of white space along both sides and the foot of each page.
  • Three inches blank at the head of page one, held for stamps from the recorder, auditor and engineer.
  • An inch and a half blank at the head of every later page.

Five categories fall outside the rule: papers from a court or a taxing authority, plats, DD-214 discharge forms, state or federal documents, and anything signed before the law took effect. The county also offers a downloadable template, which saves a title agent the trouble of guessing at margins.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Logan County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The auditor comes before the recorder

A deed visits the county auditor first, and that office shares the 100 S. Madriver Street address. The auditor's forms page lists the paperwork that can come into play:

  • Conveyance Form DTE 100 for an ordinary sale, and DTE 100M for a manufactured home.
  • Exempt Conveyance DTE 100EX, or 100MEX for a manufactured home.
  • Agriculture Conveyance DTE 102.
  • Homestead Conveyance DTE 101.
  • Owner Occupied Credit Application DTE 105C and the Homestead Exemption Application DTE 105A.
  • Destroyed Property Application DTE 26 for a building that no longer stands.

Logan County also posts a Survey and Conveyance Standards PDF for legal descriptions and an online Conveyance Fee Calculator. The state conveyance fee falls on the grantor under section 319.202. A county transfer tax joins it only where commissioners adopted one under Chapter 322. The auditor can say which charges apply to your sale.

Forfeited land sales and the recorder

A parcel that went through tax foreclosure and drew no buyer in two offerings is forfeited to the State of Ohio and remanded to the auditor. The auditor's auction rules describe a sale at the Logan County Courthouse Annex, 100 S. Madriver Street. Properties sell "As-Is" and "Buyer Beware," and the auditor makes no representation about possession, eviction or prior inspection.

The high bidder gets an Auditor's Deed. The auditor files it with the recorder and delivers it to the purchaser, and ownership passes at the moment the deed is delivered to the recorder. That deed extinguishes earlier title except for taxes and assessments not yet due, federal tax liens, easements and covenants running with the land. A delinquent taxpayer or a current owner of the parcel cannot buy.

Bidders pay everything or leave at least $1,000 per parcel on sale day, and the remainder is due within 10 calendar days. The auction rules add a 50 cent per parcel transfer charge and a 50 cent per parcel charge for envelope and postage, on top of recording.

Property taxes and reappraisal

The treasurer's office sits at 100 S. Madriver Street, Suite D, and answers at (937) 599-7223 on weekdays between 8:00 AM and 4:30 PM. The second-half bill is due each July. An automatic withdrawal option pulls the bill from a bank account on the last due date.

The county follows a six-year cycle: a reappraisal every six years, and a possible adjustment in the third calendar year after it. Taxable value is 35 percent of appraised value. The state schedule puts Logan County in a 2028 update and a 2031 reappraisal.

Challenging your value

Formal complaints go to the Board of Revision, which accepts them from January 1 through March 31. The board has three seats: the auditor, the treasurer and the president of the commissioners, or their representatives. An owner can bring appraisals or comparable sales to the hearing.

Logan County housing snapshot

Logan County lies in west central Ohio, and Bellefontaine is the seat and only city. Population reached 46,302 in July 2025. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $203,200, and 77.6 percent of housing is owner-occupied. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,326 a month, and median gross rent is $845. The county had 24,071 housing units in July 2025.

The recorder's role and Torrens land

Every Ohio county has had a recorder since the Northwest Territory of 1787. Voters have chosen the office since 1829, and a four-year term has applied since 1936.

The recorder also handles Torrens registration. Where land is registered under the Torrens Act, its boundaries are certified and a state insurance fund backs the title, and the recorder keeps those registered land records. A seller who owns an unusual rural tract should ask the Logan recorder whether any part of it was registered.

The auditor, the treasurer and the recorder all list 100 S. Madriver Street in Bellefontaine as their address, so a closing agent can take the transfer, the tax question and the recording to one building.

Typical order of a sale

The title company drafts the deed and both sides sign. The deed goes to the auditor for the conveyance form and fee, then across the building to the recorder. A seller should confirm with the treasurer that nothing is owed on the parcel before closing, since taxes follow the property.

Before you drive over, check the document against the layout list above: type size, margins, ink color and the blank space at the top of each page. Bring the fee for the page count, and call 937-599-7201 if the deed runs long and you want a total in advance. A cash sale that closes without a lender skips the payoff release, which leaves one fewer paper to record.

Frequently asked questions

What is the filing fee for a short Logan County deed?

The posted schedule charges $39 for the opening two pages, then $8 for every page after that. A document that misses the layout standards picks up $20 more.

When can I visit the Logan County recorder?

The office at 100 S. Madriver Street in Bellefontaine opens weekdays at 8:00 and closes at 4:30. Its phone number is 937-599-7201.

Which papers skip the Logan County layout fee?

Court and taxing authority papers, plats, DD-214 discharge forms and state or federal documents are exempt, along with anything executed before the law began.

Does the Logan County recorder help fill out deed forms?

The office keeps and indexes records. Have a title company or attorney draft the deed, and phone 937-599-7201 with filing questions.

When does a forfeited land buyer own the property in Logan County?

Ownership passes when the auditor hands the Auditor's Deed to the recorder. The auditor then sends the recorded deed to the purchaser.

Recorder's office in Elyria

The Lorain County Recorder files deeds. The office is in Room 102 at 226 Middle Avenue, Elyria, OH 44035. Call 440-329-5148. Weekday hours are 8 AM to 4 PM, posted on the recorder's website.

The Recorder keeps the land record and nothing else. Staff do not supply blank forms, fill them in, alter a deed, decide ownership disputes, or search for liens for you. A title company or attorney covers those jobs. County records go back to 1824. You can download a free copy of your own deed from the online property search, and certified copies are available at the counter.

What the Recorder charges

Two pages of a deed cost $39.00, and the price climbs by $8.00 with every added page. Each printed side is a page, so a deed printed on both faces of two sheets counts as four.

Lorain County Recorder charges for common filings
FilingCharge
Deed, mortgage, lease or affidavit, pages one and two$39.00

The amount splits evenly between a basic fee and a contribution to the Ohio Housing Trust Fund. A $5.00 preservation surcharge from Senate Bill 94 is part of the present level. The fee chart shows three pages at $47.00, five at $63.00 and ten at $103.00.

The auditor endorses the deed first

Under section 319.202 of the Revised Code, the buyer files a value statement, then the Auditor marks the fee on the deed. The seller pays it.

The Auditor's transfer page sets rules that trip up late arrivals:

  • Transfers happen Monday through Thursday, 8 AM to 4 PM, so Friday closings need planning.
  • E-filed packets are cut off at 3 PM, and walk-ins at 4 PM.
  • The office refuses anything sent through the U.S. Postal Service.
  • Handwritten forms go back to the sender. Typed, fully completed forms only.
  • A packet with a missing form or the wrong payment is returned, never held.

Staff may not fill out the conveyance or exempt form or give advice about it, citing section 4705.01. Your closing agent or attorney should assemble the packet and confirm the amounts with the Auditor's office in advance.

How the conveyance fee is set

Ohio law fixes the base at a one dollar minimum, or ten cents for each $100 or fraction of $100 of value, whichever is more, in section 319.54(G)(3). A county commission may add a transfer tax of as much as thirty cents per $100 under section 322.02. Phone the Auditor for the combined Lorain County rate before you estimate your net proceeds.

Many transfers owe no conveyance fee, though the form must say why. Common cases for families include gifts between spouses or from parents to children, deeds among heirs of one estate where no money is paid, and moves into or out of a revocable trust. Every transfer, exempt or not, also pays fifty cents for each parcel.

The $20 formatting charge

Documents prepared after June 30, 2009 must meet the standardization rules of section 317.114, and the Recorder adds $20.00 when they miss. The fee page spells out font size, ink color, paper size, a three inch blank band on page one and margins on every side, and offers a downloadable template. Court papers, plats, DD-214 discharges and state or federal documents are exempt.

The rules cover type size, ink, paper size and margins, and the top of page one has to stay blank for the office stamps. A deed that comes out of a title company usually meets them already. A homemade deed printed from an online form is where the problem shows up.

Have the preparer check the template before signing, since a rejected deed costs a second trip to Elyria. The Recorder does not help complete forms, so the preparer is your only safeguard here.

Lorain County housing for sellers

Lorain County stretches along Lake Erie west of Cuyahoga County. Elyria holds the courthouse, while the city of Lorain has the most residents. The county had an estimated 323,219 residents in July 2025 and 139,777 housing units. A typical owned home is worth $223,200, and owners live in 74.0 percent of homes. Median gross rent is $966. Most Lorain County sales therefore involve an owner-occupied house with a deed and mortgage already on file.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Lorain County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Guarding against deed fraud

Sign up for the free property alert service on the Recorder's website. Deed fraud means criminals transferring a property without the owner's knowledge. Check your records and be wary of unsolicited deed offers.

Before you list a house, search your own parcel online and confirm the last recorded deed carries the name of the person who will sign. If an old mortgage was paid off but its release never reached the record, have it recorded, at the $4.00 marginal notation charge.

Recording military discharge papers

An owner who served can record a DD-214 or NGB-22 so a safe copy exists if the original is lost. The records are protected, and only the person named or an authorized person can see them. One certified copy of a service discharge is free.

Keeping the deed short

Since each extra page adds $8.00, ask your preparer to keep the deed brief. A reference to an older recorded document also triggers the $4.00 notation charge. A cash sale with no lender skips the mortgage release and assignment filings, so the Recorder's bill is often just the deed.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What goes in the closing packet

Assemble these items so neither office sends you back:

  • The signed, notarized deed, typed, with the legal description and every parcel number.
  • The right conveyance form, or the exempt form with its reason written out.
  • Payment to the Auditor for the conveyance fee and the per-parcel charge.
  • A check to the Recorder sized to the page count.
  • A check that each page is in black or blue ink and has the margins the template calls for.

Because the Auditor cuts off e-files at 3 PM on transfer days, line up the vendor early on the day you close. The order is simple: the Auditor first, then the Recorder, both at 226 Middle Avenue.

Frequently asked questions

What does Lorain County charge to record a deed?

The fee page prints $39.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 per page after that. A $4.00 notation applies to each release or assignment, and a layout violation adds $20.00. The Auditor's conveyance fee is paid separately.

Will the Lorain County Auditor take a deed by mail?

No. Mailed transfers are refused. Deliver the packet in person Monday through Thursday or send it through an approved e-file vendor before 3 PM.

Can the Lorain County Recorder fix a mistake on my deed?

No. The Recorder cannot alter a deed and is not trained to search for liens for you. An attorney can prepare a corrective deed, which the Recorder then files.

Who bills property tax in Lorain County?

The County Treasurer and County Auditor handle tax bills. The Recorder only keeps the documents that show who owns the land.

Where can I see an old Lorain County deed?

Use the online property search on the Recorder's website to view and download a free copy. Records reach back to 1824, and certified copies are available in person.

Where to submit a Lucas County deed

The Lucas County Recorder works from One Government Center, Suite 700, in downtown Toledo, OH 43604. Call 419-213-4400 for the counter or write to Recorder@co.lucas.oh.us. Weekday hours are 8 AM to 4:30 PM, and electronic recording stops at 4 PM.

You can walk a deed in, mail it, or e-record through a partner company. The office strongly encourages electronic recording or mailing, and it names CSC, ePN and Simplifile as the e-recording partners. If you mail a deed, include a self addressed stamped envelope or add return postage to the payment. The office accepts cash or a check payable to the Lucas County Recorder.

Return postage for a standard one ounce first class letter is $1.00. Add that amount whenever you do not enclose a stamped envelope, since a payment that comes up short can slow intake.

Recording fees

The basic fee is $39.00 for the first two pages of a deed or mortgage and $8.00 for every extra page. The $5.00 increase behind that figure came from Senate Bill 94, and the schedule lists $39.00 as a minimum.

Lucas County Recorder fees for common items
Filing or serviceAmount
Deed or mortgage, first two pages$39.00 minimum
Each additional page$8.00
Non-compliant document (ORC 317.114)$20.00 per document
Reference for a marginal notation (release, assignment)$4.00 per reference
Real estate UCC filing$12.00 plus $4.00 per name indexed
Federal tax lien, and its release$5.00, and $3.00
Assisted photocopy$2.00 per page
Self-service photocopy$0.25 per page
Certification$1.00 per document
Military discharge (DD-214), recording or certified copyNo fee

A master mortgage reference carries no reference fee. Plats are priced by size, at ten cents per square inch with a $40.00 minimum per page.

What the Auditor charges before recording

Lucas County's Auditor publishes a real estate transfers fact sheet with two charges. The transfer fee is $0.50 per parcel. The conveyance fee is $4.00 for every $1,000 of the sale price, and some transfers outlined in law are exempt from it.

Transfers caused by a death, adding survivorship, or placing the property into your own trust are generally exempt and cost only the $0.50 per parcel. The Auditor cannot prepare a deed, and an attorney is the safer choice because a wrong detail can get the document rejected or cause trouble years later. The Auditor's main line is 419-213-4406.

The statewide rules behind these steps are in section 319.202, which requires the buyer's value statement before the Auditor endorses a deed, and section 319.54, which lists the exempt transfers.

Checking a deed online

Recorded documents after 1985 can be viewed through the Recorder's Online Recordings tool, which is run by a document technology vendor. The Auditor's AREIS property system shows deeds and transfers as public records.

AREIS shows how title is held, which helps when you are sorting out a sale after a death:

  • Property held in survivorship carries the code ORSURVTC after the owners' names.
  • Property held by a trustee shows the word Trustee after the name.
  • A transfer on death confirmation appears as document type OD on the Transfers page.

For records from before 1985, call the counter on 419-213-4400 and ask how to request a copy.

Avoid paid deed retrieval companies

Residents get solicitations from document retrieval companies that quote $49.50 to $87.00 for a certified copy of a deed. The county sells the same copy for far less. Copies of all land records are available from the office, often for as little as $2.00.

The fee schedule backs that up: assisted copies are $2.00 per page and a certification is $1.00 per document. If you have an escrow account with the office, a copy order form can be emailed to the Recorder or faxed to 419-213-4284. Copies are paid by cash, check or escrow account only.

Lucas County housing for sellers

Toledo is the county seat and largest city. The other cities are Maumee, Oregon, Sylvania and Waterville, and the villages include Holland, Ottawa Hills, Whitehouse and Swanton. The county had 423,347 residents in July 2025 and 201,974 housing units. The median owner-occupied value is $163,900, owner occupancy is 62.0 percent and median gross rent is $934. With nearly four homes in ten rented, many Lucas County sales involve a tenant-occupied house.

Other documents the Recorder files

Beyond deeds, the office accepts a full range of paperwork for the permanent land record:

  • Certificates of transfer, deeds and land contracts.
  • Mortgages, liens and real estate financing statements.
  • Plats and powers of attorney.
  • Military service discharges, and any other document made recordable by the Revised Code.

For lien paperwork the schedule gives $5.00 for a federal tax lien, $3.00 for its release and $4.00 for a personal tax release. Bureau of Workers' Compensation liens and releases carry no fee. The e-recording partners also list direct lines: CSC at 866-652-0111, ePN at 888-325-3365 extension 11234, and Simplifile at 800-460-5657 extension 1031.

How the recording fee got to $39.00

The state budget raised the fee for most documents by $6.00, to $34.00 for the first two pages, with half of all recording fees going to the Ohio Housing Trust Fund. A later $5.00 increase from Senate Bill 94 brought the figure to $39.00, under section 317.32. Counting a mailed deed's return postage in the payment avoids a delay at intake.

Title searches and older records

A title company orders the ownership search for a sale. The Recorder's online system covers documents recorded after 1985, so ask the title company how it will pull anything older.

Steps for a typical sale

The title company or an attorney drafts the deed, and you sign it. It goes to the Auditor for the value statement and the transfer and conveyance fees, then to the Recorder with the recording fee. If a lender is paid off, its release is recorded separately and each reference to the old mortgage adds the $4.00 notation charge. A cash sale skips the lender release, so there is one less filing to track. Before you head downtown, confirm the page count of the deed, because the fee is tied to it, and check that nothing on the document breaks the layout rules that bring the $20.00 charge.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

How much is the basic recording fee in Lucas County?

The schedule lists $39.00 for the first two pages of a deed or mortgage, with $8.00 for each additional page. A document that breaks the state layout rules draws a $20.00 non-compliance fee, and each reference for a marginal notation costs $4.00.

What are the Lucas County transfer and conveyance fees?

The Auditor's fact sheet shows $0.50 per parcel as the transfer fee and $4.00 for every $1,000 of the sale price as the conveyance fee. Transfers due to death, survivorship or moving the property into your own trust are generally exempt from the conveyance fee.

Does the Lucas County Recorder accept mailed deeds?

Yes. The Recorder encourages mailing and e-recording. Include a self addressed stamped envelope or add return postage to the payment, and make the check payable to the Lucas County Recorder.

Is there a fee to record a military discharge in Lucas County?

No. The fee schedule lists no fee to record a DD-214 or to get certified copies of it from the Recorder.

Can the Lucas County Auditor prepare my deed?

No. The Auditor cannot prepare transfer documents, including deeds, and recommends hiring an attorney. Staff can answer questions about the transfer process at 419-213-4406.
