The recorder's fax line is (740) 342-5539, and the auditor can be reached at (740) 342-2074. If you are sorting out several documents for one sale, calling both offices on the same day saves a second trip.

The office also sets owners up with a free fraud alert through its software vendor. A subscriber is told within 24 business hours when anything is recorded under their name. Because the office has to record any paper that meets the filing rules, the alert warns you but cannot block a filing.

Veterans can have a DD214 recorded by bringing the original or a certified copy and photo ID, and the office hands out veteran ID cards too.

What else does the Perry County recorder file?

According to the auditor, Ohio demands a full reappraisal of the county every six years, with a state percentage adjustment in the third year of each cycle. Roughly 31,000 parcels were on the books for 2024, sorted into residential, agricultural, commercial and industrial classes.

The auditor's home page also reports that House Bill 479 gives a one-time fixed reduction to current Standard and Enhanced Homestead Exemption recipients, for tax year 2026 or tax year 2027 on manufactured and mobile homes. Pickaway County, OH Recorder of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in Ohio
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Pickaway County, OH Recorder of Deeds: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is

Where do you record a deed in Pickaway County?

Deeds are recorded at the Pickaway County Recorder's Office, 110 Island Road, Suite G, Circleville, Ohio 43113, in the Pickaway County Service Center. The phone number is (740) 474-5826.

The office holds land records back to the county's start in 1810. The recorder's own words describe the job as making a clear record of deeds, mortgages, easements, plats, land surveys, powers of attorney, leases and the liens that can attach to real estate. Staff do not prepare documents and cannot say whether a title is clear.

Plan your timing. Since April 1, 2025, documents brought in after 3:30 p.m. are not recorded until the first thing on the next business day. Staff still review them and check the fees at the counter.

Can you mail or e-record a deed in Pickaway County?

Mailing works only for originals that do not need approval stamps. The recorder's page explains that the Engineer Map Department and the Auditor will not accept documents through the mail, and the recorder cannot route them. A deed that needs those stamps must be carried in, and so must a transfer on death designation.

E-recording has been offered since 2017 through a third-party vendor chosen by the submitter. Files can be sent any day, and staff process them from 8:00 a.m. to 3:45 p.m. on business days. Documents with a new survey or new legal description cannot be e-recorded and must be walked through in person.

  • Bring or mail the original with a self-addressed, stamped envelope.
  • Pay by cash, check, or card, and expect a card charge of $1.00 or 3%, whichever is greater.
  • If a deed was signed electronically and printed, a separate authenticator certificate must be attached.

What are the recording and copy fees in Pickaway County?

The base price follows the state schedule in Revised Code 317.32: $34 for the first two pages and $8 for each page after that, split between a base fee and a housing trust fund fee. Pickaway County adds the optional preservation surcharge. The recorder's page says that from January 1, 2025, basic recording fees include a $5.00 per document surcharge, which goes into the county general fund for preservation and digitization of records.

Pickaway County Recorder charges as posted on its recording, FAQ and records pages
ItemAmount
Basic recording, first two pages$34 under state law
Each added page$8 under state law
Per document surcharge since January 1, 2025$5.00

Printing images downloaded from the recorder's websiteNo charge

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Pickaway County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What does the Pickaway County auditor require before a deed is transferred?

The auditor's site states the conveyance fee as $3.00 per thousand, for real estate and manufactured homes. Under state law the seller pays it, and the auditor will not transfer an instrument without a completed DTE 100 or DTE 100EX form.

The county's Transfer and Conveyance Standards, adopted by the auditor and engineer under section 319.203, add more requirements:

  • The deed carries the original signature of the grantor and cannot be a fax or a copy.
  • It shows the auditor's parcel number, the site address, the prior deed reference and the grantee's tax mailing address.
  • A grantor who is not the prior grantee needs an explanation in the deed or an affidavit.
  • A new legal description needs the Engineer's Tax Map Department to stamp it "Mathematically Approved" first.
  • A split leaving a parcel of 20 acres or less needs planning commission approval.
  • A trust conveying property files an affidavit under section 5302.171 before or with the deed.

How do you search Pickaway County records online?

The recorder uses a site called CountyFusion. Indexes run from 1/1/1990 to the present by name, historical indexes cover 1810 to 1990, and most images go back to 1980. Official Records began on April 16, 1996, and earlier records sit in separate books for deeds, mortgages, leases and other types.

You need a name to search. If you only have an address, look up the owner on the auditor's website first. Images found online can be downloaded and printed for free, while older documents can be ordered by volume and page for $2.00 a page.

The office also offers a free alert, called FRAUDSLEUTH, that warns you when a document is recorded under names you enter. A sheriff's sale list is on the sheriff's website instead of the recorder's.

Does a paid-off mortgage show up at the Pickaway County recorder?

Yes, as a recorded release. The recorder explains that the lender sends a Release of Mortgage, which is linked to the original mortgage in the records, and you can get a copy free on the recording site or from the office.

Unlike a car title, the deed is not held by the bank or by the recorder while you owe on the loan. You should have received the original after closing, and the office can copy a recorded deed if yours is lost.

To change the tax mailing address, call the Pickaway County Treasurer at (740) 474-2370. Changing the name on a deed requires a new deed prepared by an attorney.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Pickaway County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What do Census numbers show for Pickaway County?

Pickaway County has the most residents and the highest home values of the three counties in the Census comparison used for this set of pages. The 2025 population estimate is 62,978, up 7.6% from the April 2020 estimates base, with 23,832 housing units.

  • Owner-occupied rate: 74.0%.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $256,800.
  • Median gross rent: $1,020.
  • Median household income: $74,040.
  • Building permits in 2025: 406.
  • Employer establishments in 2023: 856, with employment up 23.0% from 2022.

Compare the 406 permits with 28 in Paulding County and 39 in Perry County. Pickaway is where new construction is happening, and the county sits in the Columbus metropolitan area.

What is the Pickaway County landscape like for a house seller?

The county seat and only city is Circleville. Villages include Ashville, Commercial Point, Darbyville, Lockbourne, Harrisburg, New Holland, South Bloomfield, Tarlton and Williamsport. The Scioto River runs south through the middle of the county, Big Darby Creek drains the upper west side, and about 87% of the land is used for agriculture.

Many sales here involve acreage, so the land-split and survey rules matter. The recorder's FAQ points to the Engineer's mapping department or GIS for property maps that are not in a recorded subdivision.

One note on the recorder's page: it carried an alert about a one-time cancellation window for Homeowner Benefit Agreements with MV Realty of Ohio that ended on April 29, 2026. If you ever signed such an agreement, ask the recorder what is recorded against your parcel before you list.

Frequently asked questions

What time must I bring a document to the Pickaway County recorder?

Before 3:30 p.m. if you want it recorded that day. Documents brought in later are reviewed but not processed until the first thing the next business day.

Can a transfer on death designation be mailed to the Pickaway County recorder?

No. The recorder's page says documents that need the Engineer Map Department and Auditor stamps cannot be mailed, and it names transfer on death designations in that group.

How much is the conveyance fee in Pickaway County?

The county auditor states it as $3.00 per thousand, for both real estate and manufactured homes.

How do I get a copy of my recorded deed?

Download it free from the recorder's online site if it was recorded since the digital image coverage began, or request a copy by phone, email, mail or in person at $2.00 a page.

Does the recorder search my title for liens?

No. The office will show you how to search its records, but it cannot tell you whether title is clear. Consider a title examiner or title company for a full exam.

How do I reach the Portage County recorder in Ravenna?

The Portage County Recorder's office page prints a main line of (330) 297-3553, a fax at (330) 297-7349, and the same number for copy requests. Copy requests can also go by email to PCREC.COPIES@PORTAGECO.COM. Call before you drive a deed over to confirm counter hours.

Ravenna is the county seat, and the auditor's forms use 449 South Meridian Street as the county's address for property work. Hand-carried or mailed, a deed goes to the auditor on that street first, because the transfer there comes before recording.

Researchers should know that staff do not run the search for you. They will point you to the indexes and help you read them, and the page invites anyone studying title or family history to use the office.

What does the Portage County recorder keep on file?

The recorder's description of the office describes a permanent record of every paper that moves or burdens land here. Each filing gets a time stamp and a document number, then goes to microfilm and image storage and into the computer index.

  • Deeds, mortgages and easements.
  • Land titles and rights-of-way.
  • Federal tax liens and unemployment liens.
  • Uniform Commercial Code filings.
  • Leases of several kinds, along with veteran discharges and records of veteran burials.

Fees collected here are split between the county general fund and the state housing trust fund. The office also reminds commissioners and township trustees each year to file zoning resolutions and maps. What a seller cares about is that mortgage and lien releases appear in these same indexes, where the buyer's title examiner will look.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Portage County?

The county's fee page defers to the state schedule and gives one warning. A paper that breaks the state marginal rule picks up an added $20.00. The dollar figures below come from the statute, R.C. 317.32.

  • Pages one and two together: $34, split evenly between base and trust fund shares.
  • Every page after that: $8, again split evenly.
  • A county-set preservation surcharge, capped at $5 and paid to the general fund.
  • Certified copies: $2 per page in total.
  • Each marginal reference in a separate instrument: $4 in total.

The surcharge can be anything up to the cap, so ask the recorder for the total on your exact document. The statute counts the caption page, and any fraction of a page counts as a page.

What does the auditor take before a Portage County deed reaches the recorder?

The auditor's side comes first. According to the auditor's transfer page, the real estate department transfers deeds and similar papers ahead of recording. Its stated conveyance charge is four dollars for each $1,000 of price, plus fifty cents for every parcel moved. The DTE 100 form, Conveyance of Real Property, travels with the deed.

Use the rate Portage County prints, not a figure quoted for another county. A county board may also adopt a transfer tax on grantors of no more than 30 cents on each $100 of value, collected by the auditor ahead of recording (R.C. 322.02). Ask the auditor whether Portage has adopted one.

The same auditor's pages also offer parcel ownership histories, valuations, sales information and tax data, which are worth printing before you meet a buyer.

Which Portage County offices does a seller contact?

Three desks handle most of a sale, and each prints something different for the public.

Portage County offices a home seller usually needs, with what each published

AuditorTransfers the deed, sets the conveyance fee$4.00 per $1,000 plus 50 cents per parcel; DTE 100 form
TreasurerBills and collects property taxTwo bills a year, about half in February and half in July

The treasurer's schedule matters because the deed does not settle unpaid tax. Get a payoff for the parcel from the treasurer, and have the title company say who bears the half now accruing.

Can I search Portage County land records myself?

Yes. The recorder's page links a "Find My Deed" search, and the county posts scanned lease books on its site, with books numbered 92 through 114 posted so far and more promised as scanning continues. The office warns that its indexes default to one page for some older volumes and pages, so documents shown as a single page may run longer. Call or email the office for correct page totals before you order copies.

Copies of all records are available on request. Bring a parcel number or the names on the deed, since staff will not search on your behalf. The auditor's property search gives the owner history and sales for a parcel, which narrows what to ask for.

The state's rule on documents also applies here: Ohio requires a conveyance to be prepared and signed under the Revised Code before it is accepted for record. The recorder's page says so in plain terms.

What should I have ready before I record in Portage County?

Bring a deed that was prepared and signed under the Ohio Revised Code, since the recorder's page says all documents to be recorded must be. Have the auditor's transfer done first, and keep the DTE 100 form with the paperwork.

  • The signed, acknowledged deed with the marginal rule observed.
  • Payment for the auditor's conveyance fee and the recorder's fees.
  • A parcel number, so staff and the online index can match the right record.

After acceptance the office stamps the time, numbers the document, films and scans it, and adds it to the index. After closing, request a copy of the recorded deed for your own file.

What else should a Portage County seller know about recording?

The county covers 504 square miles of Northeast Ohio and dates to an 1808 act of the General Assembly, per its about page. The 2020 population as 161,791 and puts rented homes at 31.1% of the occupied total.

  • Format the deed to Ohio's page and margin rules to avoid the $20 surcharge.
  • Record a mortgage satisfaction soon after payoff, so the buyer's title search is clean.
  • Visit the auditor for the transfer step before the recorder.

The recorder's office has also listed a Good Deeds Program, billed as a way to prepare now and avoid the probate court process later. Ask the office for current dates and locations if a family property may pass to heirs.

A house with liens, back taxes or a stalled estate can still be sold for cash, and the buyer's closing agent handles the filings.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Portage County recorder's phone number?

The main line is (330) 297-3553, and the fax is (330) 297-7349. Copy requests use the same phone number and also go by email to PCREC.COPIES@PORTAGECO.COM.

How much does the Portage County auditor charge to transfer a deed?

Four dollars per $1,000 of the price plus fifty cents a parcel, according to the auditor. The recorder's fee is separate, and the auditor's transfer happens first.

Is there an extra recording fee in Portage County?

Yes, in one case. A paper that breaks the state marginal rule picks up $20.00 on top of the usual charges, so check margins before you submit.

Can I look up a Portage County deed online?

Yes. The recorder's page links a Find My Deed search, and the auditor's real estate site shows ownership history and sales. The recorder warns that page counts on older volumes can be wrong, so confirm them by phone.

Does the recorder pay off my mortgage or my taxes?

No. The recorder files papers and nothing more. Payoffs run through your lender and the county treasurer, and a closing agent normally arranges both.

Where do I record a deed in Preble County, Ohio?

The Preble County Recorder sits on the second floor of the courthouse, 101 E. Main Street, Eaton, OH 45320, phone (937) 456-8173. The recorder's page lists weekday service until 4:30 in the afternoon, yet the courthouse front door is locked at 4:00, so get there early.

Eaton is the county seat. Wikipedia dates the county to February 15, 1808, carved from Butler and Montgomery Counties, and gives it 426 square miles and a 2020 population of 40,999. About three in four residents live in rural areas.

16,412 households and 18,093 housing units in the county, 9.3% of them vacant, with 76.7% of occupied homes lived in by their owners. That ownership rate means most Preble County deeds pass between owner-occupants, so expect questions about the grantee's tax mailing address and marital status at the counter. Check with the office about holiday hours before you plan a trip around a closing date.

What does it cost to record a deed in Preble County?

The county's printed schedule is short. One flat price covers a deed, mortgage, affidavit, easement, land contract, lease, mechanic's lien, trust or power of attorney: $39.00 through page two, then $8.00 for every added page. A marginal notation is $4.00.

  • Certified copies are $2.00 per page, with $1.00 more for each seal.
  • A document that misses Ohio's standardization rules in R.C. 317.114 costs $20.00 more.
  • Court, tax authority, state and federal documents, plats and DD 214 discharges are exempt from that $20.00, as are papers signed before July 1, 2009.
  • Filing a military discharge, or getting a photocopy of one, is free.

The state fee statute, R.C. 317.32, makes up the two-page figure from two $17 shares plus an optional preservation charge of up to $5, which is how a county arrives at $39. Enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope if you want the recorded paper returned by mail.

How should a Preble County deed be formatted?

The county spells out its formatting rules, and following them avoids the surcharge. Use white paper, letter or legal size, with black or blue ink and type of 10 point or larger. Submit an original rather than a copy, and skip highlighting and white-out.

  • Keep three inches clear at the top of page one for the recorder, auditor and engineer stamps.
  • Keep an inch and a half clear at the top of later pages, and an inch at the sides and bottom.
  • Show who prepared the document, and type or print a name below any signature that is hard to read.
  • State the grantor's marital status, and give the grantee's tax mailing address.
  • Include a full legal description and prior recording information, approved by the engineer before recording.

The grantor signs and acknowledges the deed before a notary public. The conveyance document must also carry the stamps of the county engineer and county auditor showing the grantor complied with R.C. 319.202.

What does the Preble County auditor charge on a sale?

The recorder's page puts the auditor's conveyance fee at three dollars for each $1,000 of price, with a 50 cent transfer fee per parcel. The auditor's counter is on the second floor of the same courthouse, (937) 456-8148, and the deed is stamped there before it goes to the recorder.

A county commission may also adopt a transfer tax of up to 30 cents per $100, which R.C. 322.02 assigns to the grantor and routes through the auditor. Before you total your net proceeds, ask whether Preble County has adopted one.

The county's Office of Land Use Management, at 937-456-8171 on the first floor, answers questions about property splits and building permits. A lot split matters if you are selling only part of a parcel, since the engineer must approve the legal description.

Which Preble County offices handle a home sale?

All three main offices share the courthouse, so a seller can finish most of the errands in one trip.

Preble County courthouse offices for a home sale, with phone numbers as printed on the county's own pages
OfficeUsed forPhone
RecorderRecording deeds, mortgages and releases(937) 456-8173
AuditorConveyance fee, transfer, valuation complaints(937) 456-8148
TreasurerPaying property tax(937) 456-8140

Per the county FAQ, tax payments are taken on the second floor at the treasurer's office. The sheriff's office handles sheriff's sales on Fridays at 9 a.m. in the first-floor lobby of the courthouse, which is where a foreclosure sale of a Preble County home would be held.

How do I search Preble County land records?

The recorder offers an online search index, a title fraud service and a fraud sleuth profile through its page. The county's note on its records says indexes available online start December 14, 1999, through a CountyFusion site, and the Ohio Recorders Association page for Preble County links to the same system. For older deeds, you need to visit the office or ask staff.

The same page describes the recorder's purpose as a complete, accurate and permanent record of documents that convey or burden land, used by attorneys, historians, genealogists and land title examiners. If you are tracing an old farm or a family transfer, ask for the volume and page once you find the entry in the index.

Owners who are worried about forged deeds can register for the free title fraud service the page links.

Can the Preble County Board of Revision change my value before I sell?

It can lower or raise a value, but only on a complaint filed inside the window. The auditor's Board of Revision page takes the DTE Form 1 in the first quarter after the tax year, with a cutoff of 4:30 in the afternoon on March 31 at the auditor's office. Mail counts if it is postmarked by that day.

Three people sit on the Board: the auditor, the treasurer and a commissioner or the commissioner's representative. The page cites R.C. 5715.13 through 5715.19 for its authority. Questions go to (937) 456-8197 or (937) 456-8131. A late or defective complaint may be dismissed without a hearing, so file early.

Where do other Preble County matters go besides the recorder?

A sale sometimes pulls in other offices, and the county's FAQ sorts out who handles what. Evictions and small claims are heard by the Eaton Municipal Court at 1199 Preble Drive, phone 937-456-4941. Probate Court, second floor, 937-456-8137, handles name changes and marriage licenses. The Clerk of Courts has the third floor, 937-456-8160.

Sheriff's sales run on Fridays beginning at 9 a.m. in the first-floor lobby, and the sheriff's office at 937-456-6262 has details. A seller facing one of those sales or a tenant dispute can still deal with the recorder and auditor in the usual order, but should line up the court side first.

Frequently asked questions

How much does the Preble County recorder charge for a deed?

$39.00 covers the first two pages and each added page is $8.00. A marginal notation is another $4.00, and a nonconforming paper adds $20.00.

What is the Preble County conveyance fee?

Three dollars per $1,000 of price plus fifty cents a parcel, as the recorder's page prints it, paid to the auditor ahead of recording.

What time does the Preble County recorder's office close?

Service runs to 4:30 on weekdays, but the courthouse front door locks at 4:00. Get there before 4:00, or call (937) 456-8173 if you are running late.

Can I get my DD 214 from the Preble County recorder?

Yes. Military discharge papers are kept at the recorder's office, and filing a discharge or getting a photocopy of it carries no fee.

When does the Preble County Board of Revision take complaints?

From January 1 to March 31 of the year after the tax year, with a cutoff of 4:30 in the afternoon on March 31 at the auditor's office. Mailed ones need a postmark by then.

Where is the Putnam County recorder in Ottawa?

The Putnam County Recorder works from 245 E. Main Street in Ottawa, the same street address the county auditor lists. The recorder's resources page gives a phone of 419.523.6490, a toll-free line at 888.638.0042 and a fax at 419.523.4403.

The office opens at 8:30 and closes at 4:30 on weekdays, while the recording window shuts at 4:15. The contact page also lists the days the office closes: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Day, Presidents Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas.

Ottawa is the county seat. An 1820 creation date, an 1834 organization date, and a name honoring Israel Putnam. The Blanchard River, an early travel route for settlers, crosses the county.

In what sequence does a Putnam County deed get recorded?

Three stops come before the recorder sees a deed, and the county auditor's page spells them out. The order matters, because an unstamped deed is turned away.

  1. Take the legal description to the Tax Map Office, which sits in the engineer's office and answers at 419-523-6931. All legal descriptions must be pre-approved, and the document must meet the county's conveyance standards.
  2. Once the tax map staff sign the document, bring it to the auditor, who transfers it and collects the conveyance fee.
  3. Record the transferred deed with the recorder, who follows the standards and fees on its own site.

The auditor is at 245 East Main Street in Ottawa, 419-523-6686, on a weekday 8:30 to 4:30 schedule. Under Tools on its site sits a calculator that prices the transfer before you go.

What does the Putnam County auditor charge to transfer a deed?

On its transfers page the auditor lists four dollars for each thousand of price, with the price rounded up to the next hundred, and fifty cents a parcel in transfer fee. The conveyance is not processed unless the check matches the conveyance fee to the penny.

Form DTE 100 accompanies a normal sale, and DTE 100 (EX) is the version for deeds that claim an exemption. The county's forms page carries both, so you can fill them in ahead of the visit.

A separate county transfer tax is possible under R.C. 322.02, capped at 30 cents on each $100 and owed by the grantor. Whether Putnam has one in force is a question for the auditor; the calculator gives the quickest total.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Putnam County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How much does recording cost in Putnam County?

The recorder's FAQ points to a fee page and says the office charges a $4.00 fee for each marginal notation. The base amounts come from the statute, R.C. 317.32.

  • Pages one and two: $34 together, half base fee and half housing trust fund.
  • Later pages: $8 each, split the same way.
  • A preservation surcharge, capped at $5 an instrument, goes to the county's general fund.
  • A certified copy costs $2 a page in total.

A document that fails the county's standards costs $20 more. Those rules, under R.C. 317.114, call for 10-point type or larger, dark blue or black ink, no highlighter, and letter or legal paper. Page one needs three inches clear at the top, later pages an inch and a half, and the sides and bottom an inch. Exempt are court papers, plats, DD 214 discharges, state and federal documents, and anything signed before July 1, 2009.

Which Putnam County offices matter in a home sale?

The table sets out what each office prints for the public, drawn from the county's own sites.

Putnam County offices a seller visits, with figures as published on the recorder and auditor sites
OfficeStep in a salePublished detail
Tax Map OfficePre-approves the legal description419-523-6931, located in the engineer's office
AuditorTransfers the deed, collects the conveyance feeFour dollars per $1,000 and 50 cents a parcel; 419-523-6686
RecorderRecords the deed and mortgage releases419.523.6490; recording hours 8:30 to 4:15

The auditor's home page also posts a delinquent real estate list and counts 29,689 parcels as of 2023. Sellers with a house that may have fallen behind should check that list.

How can I record a Putnam County deed electronically or by mail?

The recorder's e-recording page says the service now covers deeds and other transfer documents, and names three approved vendors: Simplifile at 1.800.460.5657, CSC at 1.866.652.0111 and Erecording Partners at 1.888.325.3365. You work through one of them rather than the county directly.

The FAQ describes how fast things move. Documents recorded at the counter go back immediately, documents e-recorded are returned immediately, and documents delivered by mail are sent out the next business day. The office also requires a full legal description, including on releases and assignments, and maintains tract indexing by geography.

Paying at the counter is simple: the FAQ says checks are made payable to the Putnam County Recorder. The same page says releases and assignments need a full legal description too, so a mortgage satisfaction needs more than a parcel number. If you are mailing a paper, allow for the next-business-day return and for the time the auditor's transfer takes first.

Records search is online. The FAQ says the indexes are open to everyone, viewing images needs a free online subscriber form, and documents are indexed on the computer starting January 1, 1993. A recording notification service is also offered.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Putnam County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What tools does the Putnam County auditor's site offer sellers?

Its Tools menu holds these items:

  • Sales reports and delinquency reports.
  • The conveyance calculator.
  • A tax estimator.

A GIS parcel viewer sits behind the Map link, and an Info section holds the forms the state and the office provide.

The same page posts the 2025 delinquent parcels list. Search your parcel before listing, and phone the auditor if the record looks off.

What else does the Putnam County recorder do?

Beyond deeds, the office runs the county's Ohio Century Farm registrations. A farm qualifies after 100 years in one family, and the recorder will meet with a family to check eligibility. It also keeps military discharge records, which are the DD 214 files veterans need for benefits.

Putnam County is mostly rural. Wikipedia's 2020 figures: 34,451 people over 484 square miles, with 84.2% living in rural areas and owners occupying 83.8% of occupied homes. The county board of education operates nine school districts.

Long-held land is a point of pride here. A farm owned by one family for 100 years can be registered, and qualified registrants receive an heirloom certificate signed by the Governor and the Director of the Ohio Department of Agriculture. A yard sign is available for purchase. The recorder will meet with you to check eligibility, so ask before you sell a farm that might qualify.

12,976 households and 13,824 housing units in the county, 6.1% of them vacant.

A farm, an estate home or a house with a balance owed still goes through the same paperwork, and a cash buyer can purchase it in present condition and cover these fees at the closing table.

Frequently asked questions

What are the Putnam County recorder's hours?

Doors are open weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30, with recording accepted from 8:30 to 4:15. The office closes on the holidays its contact page lists.

What does the Putnam County auditor charge for a deed transfer?

Four dollars per thousand of price, rounded up to the next hundred, plus fifty cents a parcel. The check has to equal the conveyance fee exactly.

Do I need approval before I bring a deed to the Putnam County recorder?

Yes. The Tax Map Office in the engineer's office must clear the legal description, and the auditor must transfer the deed before it reaches the recorder.

Does Putnam County accept e-recorded deeds?

Yes. E-recording now covers deeds and transfer documents, through the vendors the recorder lists: Simplifile, CSC and Erecording Partners.

How much is a marginal notation in Putnam County?

$4.00 for each one, per the recorder's FAQ. A nonconforming document costs $20.00 more.

Richland County, OH Recorder of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in Ohio
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Richland County, OH Recorder of Deeds: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is

Selling in Richland County?

Where the Richland County Recorder is and what it does

The Richland County Recorder keeps the public record of who owns land in the county and which liens and mortgages sit on it. The counter is in the county building at 50 Park Avenue East, Mansfield. It opens on weekdays at 8:00 AM, closes at 4:00 PM, and takes no new filings after 3:45 PM. Call 419-774-5602.

Each filing is indexed so a title examiner can trace ownership from one holder to the next. For a seller, the recorder is the last stop. Once the buyer's deed is recorded, the transfer becomes part of the public record.

Richland County has 54,904 housing units and 124,893 residents. Median monthly owner costs are $1,218 with a mortgage and $489 without. Land runs from Mansfield, Ontario and Shelby out to the villages and townships, and all of it is recorded at this one counter.

Steps to record a deed

Deeds pass through several county offices before they are recorded. A typical sequence looks like this.

  • Sign and acknowledge the deed. Sign it, then acknowledge the signature before an officer section 5301.01 allows: a notary, a judge, a court clerk, the county auditor or engineer, or a mayor.
  • Request tax map pre-approval by email to taxmap@richlandcountyoh.gov. Pre-approval must be included with any electronic deed transfer for real estate.
  • At the Auditor's counter, file the conveyance statement, pay the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax, and get the endorsement.
  • Hand the endorsed deed and the recording fee to the Recorder ahead of the 3:45 PM cutoff.

Electronic deed transfers are accepted. Anything the Tax Map Office and the Auditor must review still has to be carried to the courthouse. Staff do not hand out legal forms and point people to an attorney for drafting help. Most sellers never make this trip themselves, because the closing attorney or title company walks the deed through each counter.

Why the Tax Map Office looks at your deed

The Tax Map Office is a division of the Richland County Engineer's Office, and it keeps the property map for every deeded parcel for the auditor. Its services include checking all recorded deeds, maintaining current maps with ownership, providing copies of surveys and checking surveys done in the county. Phone 419-774-5620. The counter keeps the same weekday schedule as the rest of the building.

Because the office checks deeds against its maps, a seller who is splitting a lot or changing a legal description should raise it with tax map staff before the closing date. A change that surfaces on the day of closing can hold up the whole transaction.

Richland County offices a deed passes through

County AuditorReceives the conveyance statement and endorses the deed419-774-5501
County TreasurerTakes payment of conveyance fees and shows any tax owed419-774-5622
County RecorderRecords and indexes the deed419-774-5602
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Richland County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What the Auditor requires before recording

Section 319.202 requires the buyer or a representative to submit a statement of the property's value first. Only then does the auditor endorse the deed. The statement carries two affirmations. One asks whether the seller's bill carried a reduction such as homestead or owner occupancy. The other asks about CAUV farm valuation, since land that drops out can owe recoupment under section 5713.34.

The seller, as grantor, pays the conveyance fee set in section 319.54(G)(3). A commissioner-adopted transfer tax under Chapter 322 falls on the seller as well. The ceiling for that county tax is thirty cents per hundred dollars of value, and the auditor collects it when the deed is delivered, before recording. Conveyance fees are paid at the treasurer's office. Ask the Auditor what applies to your sale before setting a closing date.

Value means the whole consideration, any mortgage or vendor's lien included, and willful misstatement is forbidden.

Recording fees

Recording fees are set by Ohio law. The schedule starts with a seventeen dollar base fee and a seventeen dollar housing trust fund fee for the first two pages, and each added page carries four dollars of each. A preservation surcharge of up to five dollars is optional for counties (section 317.32). Certified copies and photocopies carry their own per-page charges under the same section.

Page count moves the total, so confirm the amount for your own document by phone. Use 419-774-5602 before sending any payment. A check that comes up short can mean the deed is returned and the closing slips.

Searching Richland County land records

A link on the recorder's website opens an online records search where deeds, mortgages and releases can be read. This is useful for a seller checking whether an old mortgage was ever released, or whether a prior owner's lien is still on file.

The auditor's property search adds parcel data, and the Land Bank at 50 Park Avenue East, lower level 1, acquires vacant and abandoned properties. Heirs who plan to sell should check that the last recorded deed names the person who holds title. If it names a parent or grandparent, talk to an attorney or title company about clearing that before you list.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Richland County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Older deeds without witnesses

Usually they still count. A deed signed before February 1, 2002 without the two witnesses the earlier law asked for is still deemed properly executed under section 5301.01(B), absent fraud in obtaining the signature. Recording it with the recorder of the land's county puts later buyers and lenders on notice.

The rule protects families holding old deeds. It does not fix a missing acknowledgment on a newly signed deed, so a current deed still needs the notary or other officer named in the statute.

Who decides on a transfer tax?

The board of county commissioners does. Under section 322.02, a county may levy a real property transfer tax by resolution, after two public hearings held three to ten days apart with newspaper, website or public notice sites carrying notice for two consecutive weeks. The resolution is subject to referendum unless adopted as an emergency measure by a unanimous vote. The commissioners may also send the question to voters, and then it takes effect only if a majority approves. Because the rate is a local choice, always ask the Auditor for the figure that applies to your closing.

Before you head to closing

A short checklist keeps a Richland County sale on schedule. Confirm who signs the deed and that the notary is available. Ask the title company whether tax map pre-approval is done. Get the conveyance fee and any transfer tax figure from the Auditor. Have the recording fee ready for the Recorder. If a mortgage is being paid off, the lender records its release as a separate document, and the title company tracks that for you.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, but the deed still takes the same path through the Tax Map Office, the Auditor and the Recorder.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Richland County Recorder located?

It is at 50 Park Avenue East in Mansfield, Ohio 44902, phone 419-774-5602. Filings stop at 3:45 PM on weekdays.

Is tax map approval needed before a Richland County deed is recorded?

Yes for electronic deed transfers. Tax map pre-approval must come with the deed, and taxmap@richlandcountyoh.gov is the address to request it.

Can I record a Richland County deed online?

Partly. Electronic deed transfers are accepted, while documents needing Tax Map and Auditor review go in person. Call 419-774-5602 to confirm which route fits your document.

Which party covers the conveyance fee on a Richland County sale?

The grantor, meaning the seller. The seller owes it along with any county transfer tax, paid before recording.

Will the Richland County Recorder supply legal forms?

No. Staff do not supply legal forms and suggest asking an attorney.

Where the Ross County Recorder's office is

You will find the office in the courthouse, 2 North Paint Street, Suite E, Chillicothe, Ohio 45601. Its number is 740-702-3000. Documents sent by mail go to PO Box 6162, Chillicothe, OH 45601, and the office email is rossrec@bright.net. The treasurer's office is next door in Suite F, so a tax balance and a recording can be handled in one trip.

Ross County has 76,429 residents and 32,165 housing units, and owners occupy 69.6% of homes. Median home value among owners is $171,500. Much of the county is wooded hills with farmland between them, so any sale of acreage should be checked with the auditor for farm valuation before the deed is signed. A farm that straddles a county line has its deed recorded wherever each piece of land lies.

What it costs to record a deed

The fee sheet, dated January 1, 2025, prices a document by its page count. A one or two page document is $39.00, a three page one is $47.00, and every added page is another $8.00. Documents that fall outside the standard format under section 317.114 carry a $20.00 surcharge, and each marginal reference adds $4.00. The office notes that recording fees are set by the Ohio Legislature.

The schedule continues to 88 pages at $727.00 and then adds $8.00 for each page beyond that.

State law sets the pattern: a base fee plus an equal housing trust fund fee, with an optional preservation surcharge of up to five dollars (section 317.32). A postage-paid, self-addressed envelope is required with every filing, so include one when you mail a deed.

Other recorder charges

  • A certified copy runs $5.00 for page one and $2.00 for every page after it.
  • Ordinary copies are $2.00 per printed page, with $7 for a two-page document and $9 for three pages.
  • Fax charges are $2.00 a page to a local or toll-free number and $4.00 a page to a toll number.
  • No one needs the original recorded deed to sell or borrow, because a certified copy from the office serves equally well.

These charges apply to documents the office handles after a sale, such as copying a recorded deed for a title company or an heir.

Searching records online and avoiding copy scams

Most records go back to January 1, 1974 and further, and can be viewed and downloaded free from home through the county's CountyFusion search. The office also assists people in person while they wait. Anyone can look up a deed, mortgage or release this way before listing a house.

Watch for private companies that mail letters or turn up in online searches charging $79.99 to $99.99 for copies of a deed. These companies are not government offices, and the same records are free to view at the courthouse offices. The recorder calls those offers a scam for money and recommends skipping them.

One exception applies to military discharge papers: a DD214 is not a full public record, and only the discharged service member, a military service office or a funeral director handling burial services can get an unredacted certified copy, free of charge.

What must happen before a deed reaches the recorder

Start with signing and acknowledgment. Section 5301.01 names who may take the acknowledgment, including a notary public, judge, court clerk, county auditor, county engineer or mayor. The auditor comes next. After the buyer files a value statement under section 319.202, the Ross County Auditor endorses the deed. The statement asks whether the seller's taxes had been cut by a program such as homestead, and whether the land sat in the farm valuation program, which can carry a recoupment charge.

Before the deed goes across the hall, the seller pays the auditor the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax. Section 322.02 lets a county set that transfer tax as high as thirty cents per hundred dollars of value. The Ross County Auditor knows the figure that applies.

Property tax and your closing

Ross County collects real estate tax one year behind. Taxes attach to the property and not to its owner, so a new buyer can receive a bill soon after purchase, and the closing papers normally credit the buyer with the prorated share. Payments come due in two installments, in February and August, and the treasurer can supply the exact days. Get the balance in writing and hand it to the title company.

If back taxes are owed, the treasurer's Delinquent Tax Contract splits them into five equal installments, and the SMART Payments Program spreads them over 30 months or longer. A seller with a contract open should confirm what balance stays with the property. A 5% late charge applies when payment is received within ten days and 10% after that.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Ross County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

An old family deed without two witnesses

Ohio treats most such deeds as valid. For an instrument signed before February 1, 2002 and never witnessed by two people as the earlier statute asked, section 5301.01(B) presumes it properly executed unless fraud produced the signature. Once the deed is filed with the recorder, later buyers and lenders have notice of it. Heirs who find a mid-century deed in a drawer should still check that it was actually recorded, because the index at the recorder's office is what a title company searches.

A quick path for a seller

For a sale, the order is simple. The seller signs before a notary. The buyer's side files the value statement with the auditor, and the seller pays the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax. The endorsed deed then goes to the recorder with the fee for its page count and a return envelope if it is mailed. A cash buyer follows the same path, and the only difference is that no lender waits on the recording.

If you are handling the filing yourself, bring the signed and acknowledged deed, the auditor's endorsement, a payment sized to the page count, and the return envelope. Call 740-702-3000 first if the deed runs long or has an unusual format, since a document outside the standard layout adds a $20.00 surcharge. Once it is recorded, ask for a certified copy for your files, since it serves in place of the original for later sales or loans.

Frequently asked questions

What does a short deed cost to record in Ross County?

$39.00 under the fee sheet that took effect January 1, 2025. Pages past the second add $8.00 each, and non-standard documents add $20.00.

What address takes a mailed Ross County deed?

Send it to PO Box 6162, Chillicothe, OH 45601, with payment and the postage-paid return envelope the office requires on every filing.

Can I view Ross County records without paying a service?

Yes. Most records back to January 1, 1974 can be viewed and downloaded free through the county's CountyFusion site. Copies made in the office are $2.00 per printed page.

Must I hold the original deed to sell in Ross County?

No. A certified copy from the recorder is as good as the original for a sale or a mortgage. Page one of a certified copy is $5.00, and later pages are $2.00 each.

Which office endorses a Ross County deed before recording?

The County Auditor does, after the buyer files a statement of value. The seller settles the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax with the auditor first.

Reaching the Sandusky County Recorder

The Sandusky County Recorder keeps the land records from Room 143 of the building at 100 N. Park Ave. in Fremont, ZIP 43420. The counter opens at 8:00 AM and closes at 4:30 PM, Monday to Friday. Dial (419) 334-6226 with questions. The first deed went on record on May 16, 1822, so the files span two centuries of Sandusky County ownership.

Staff index every instrument by name and parcel. A title examiner uses that index to trace a chain of owners and to spot any mortgage or lien still attached. For a copy of something already recorded, email the recorder's staff through the county site.

Fremont is the county seat, and Bellevue and Clyde are the other two cities. Whichever town your house sits in, including Gibsonburg and Woodville, the paper trail ends at the same Fremont counter.

The path a deed follows from signing to the record

Think of it as two counters on one floor. The auditor works first, in Room 109, phone (419) 334-6123. The recorder works second, in Room 143, and only the recorder's stamp puts the deed into the public index.

  • A new deed is drafted with the full legal description, which you can lift from the previous deed shown in the county's online land search.
  • The grantor signs before a notary, or another official Ohio law names for this purpose.
  • The auditor receives the deed along with the state's value statement, collects its fees, and endorses the deed.
  • The recorder takes the endorsed deed, collects the recording charge, and returns the original as you direct.

Closing attorneys and title companies commonly carry the paperwork for you. If you are giving a house to a relative instead of selling it, ask the auditor which exemption form fits before you drive downtown.

Ohio statutes on valid and protected deeds

Two short sections do most of the work. R.C. 5301.01 says the grantor signs and that the signature is acknowledged before a court judge or clerk, a county auditor or engineer, a notary or a mayor, who then certifies it. A deed without that certificate is not ready to file.

R.C. 5301.25 deals with priority. It sends land instruments to the recorder of the county where the parcel sits. Until a deed is filed there, a later purchaser who paid honestly and knew nothing of it can treat the earlier deed as fraudulent. A seller should confirm filing after closing.

The same section adds a rule for deeds that follow a survey: the surveyor's name must appear in the deed. Ask your closing agent whether yours needs that wording.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Sandusky County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Recording fees

The base recording charges come from R.C. 317.32, where every charge is split into two equal halves. A county can layer a preservation surcharge on top, so the counter total may run higher than the statute's figures. Phone the recorder for the posted schedule first.

Recording fees under R.C. 317.32
ServiceBase feeHousing trust fund fee
Recording and indexing, first two pages$17$17
Every added page (8.5 by 14 inches or part of one)$4$4
Certified copy, each page$1$1
Photocopy made after recording, each page$1$1
Marginal reference in a separate instrument$2$2

The surcharge, capped at five dollars, goes into the county general fund. Payment is due at presentation, though an e-recording submitter may settle by electronic funds transfer afterward.

Who pays transfer charges when a house sells?

The seller does. The buyer's side files a value statement with the auditor under R.C. 319.202, and the grantor covers the state conveyance fee plus any local tax a county has adopted under Chapter 322.

The state fee in R.C. 319.54(G)(3) is whichever is larger: $1, or ten cents for every $100 of value, with any leftover part of $100 counting as a full unit. R.C. 322.02 lets commissioners adopt a further tax capped at thirty cents per hundred. Ask the Sandusky County Auditor what combined rate applies on your recording date.

The same statute exempts many transfers. A sampling:

  • deeds that only give or release security for a debt
  • corrective deeds that fix one already recorded
  • gifts passing between spouses or from parents to children
  • transfers ordered by a court that are not themselves sales
  • conveyances among the heirs of a single decedent where no money changes hands

An exempt deed still needs a written reason, which the state's DTE 100(EX) form captures.

Electronic filing

The recorder accepts electronic filings. A filer signs up with one of four approved providers on the county's vendor sheet: ePN, CSC eRecording, Simplifile or Hopdox. Lenders, attorneys and title offices typically hold an account with at least one.

Without a title office you can still file by hand. The county's public search link on the recorder page is a useful first stop, since it lets you copy your own legal description and check what is already of record against the parcel.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Sandusky County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Sandusky County housing in brief

The county has an estimated 58,655 residents and 26,530 housing units holding 24,686 households. About 73.4 percent of units are owner-occupied, the typical owned home is valued at $160,700, and typical rent is $783 a month. Because about three in four homes have their owner living inside, most competing listings are owner-occupied houses.

The Sandusky River cuts northeast through the county toward Sandusky Bay on Lake Erie, so a parcel near the water deserves a flood-zone check from your title office.

Property taxes at closing

Bills fall due on the third Friday of February and the second Friday of July, and the treasurer can move a date when the state changes the schedule, as happened under House Bill 186. Check the date printed on your own bill.

Your closing agent requests the owed amount from the treasurer and holds it back from your proceeds. When a half-year is still open, get the treasurer's payoff number before you commit to a contract. The treasurer's site also links to sheriff sale listings and the county land bank, worth a look if the house passed through a tax foreclosure.

A cash buyer still wants the payoff in hand, so request it early and keep the written figure with your closing papers.

On the day of closing, expect the title company to collect your signature on the deed before a notary, the value statement, and any exemption form. Afterward the deed goes to the auditor and then the recorder, and you should ask for confirmation once it is on record. If you sold by mail or from out of town, the title office can arrange the notary and handle the filing without you visiting Fremont.

Frequently asked questions

Which office records Sandusky County deeds?

The Sandusky County Recorder, Room 143 at 100 N. Park Ave. in Fremont. The phone is (419) 334-6226.

Which counter comes first, auditor or recorder?

The auditor. It reviews the value statement, takes its fees, and endorses the deed. The recorder accepts the instrument after that step, so plan your visits in that order.

What is the statutory cost of filing a deed here?

For the first two pages R.C. 317.32 pairs a $17 recording fee with an equal $17 for the state housing trust fund; every page after that carries a $4 and $4 pair. Counties can tack on up to $5 more, so ask the recorder what the full charge is.

Can a deed be recorded electronically in Sandusky County?

Yes, through ePN, CSC eRecording, Simplifile or Hopdox, the four providers on the county's vendor sheet. Title offices and attorneys usually file this way.

What risk comes with leaving a deed unrecorded?

An unrecorded deed loses ground to a later buyer who pays in good faith and has no notice of it, because R.C. 5301.25 labels the earlier instrument fraudulent as to that buyer.

Scioto County, OH Recorder of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Where to record a deed in Scioto County

Deeds for Scioto County land are recorded at the Scioto County Recorder's Office, 602 7th St., Room 110, Portsmouth, Ohio 45662. Counter service starts at 8:00 am on weekdays and stops at 4:00 pm; the line is (740) 355-8304. Portsmouth is the county seat, and the auditor and treasurer have offices at that same 7th Street address.

You can file in person or by mail. Mail filers should enclose a self-addressed stamped envelope. Without one, the office charges postage to send the original back.

Paying the recorder and formatting the document

The recorder takes cash or a check, and nothing else. Make the check payable to "Scioto County Recorder", because checks written to a second or third party are refused. Scioto County has also adopted the $5.00 record preservation fee on top of its other recording charges.

A deed must meet these layout rules before it will be accepted:

  • Legible type of size ten or larger, in blue or black ink only
  • Letter or legal size sheets (8 1/2 by 11, or 8 1/2 by 14)
  • No highlighted text
  • One inch margins at the sides and bottom
  • Three blank inches above the text on page one, and an inch and a half above it on every later page

A deed that misses these rules can be turned away, which delays your closing. Have the attorney or title agency preparing the deed check them before signing.

The order a deed travels

The recorder's checklist reads like this: write the deed on a fresh form rather than copying the old one, borrow the legal description from the last recorded deed, have a notary witness the signing, take the transfer to the Scioto County Auditor, and bring the deed back to the recorder once that office is done.

The auditor bills a transfer charge of its own, apart from the recorder's. That counter is Room 103 (740.355.8264) and stays open until 4:30 pm.

Two related points matter to sellers. After a payoff, the lender files a release of mortgage as its own document, and no new deed appears. And mobile home titles are not kept at the recorder, because they are registered with the county auditor.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Scioto County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Auditor transfer charges

The auditor's transfer charges come from R.C. 319.54(G), and Chapter 322 allows an added county transfer tax. The county's full recording fee list is a separate sheet, so request it from the recorder before sending payment.

Auditor fees under R.C. 319.54(G)
Auditor serviceFee
Transfer or entry of a lot or parcel of landFifty cents for each transfer or entry, paid by the person requiring it
Receiving the statement of value (conveyance fee)One dollar, or ten cents for each one hundred dollars or fraction, whichever is greater
Deed of land sold for taxesFive dollars, paid by the purchaser

Section 319.54(G)(3) excuses certain deeds from the conveyance fee: those given only as security for a debt, corrective deeds, and no-money transfers between heirs are examples. An excused deed travels with a short statement of the reason.

What the Recorder cannot do for you

The office does not draft documents or offer legal advice. A fill-in-the-blank form still requires choices that count as legal advice.

  • It cannot tell you whether you hold good and clear title. Title examiners search the recorder's index and other county offices to decide that.
  • It does not remove or release liens. A federal tax lien is recorded there, but only the issuing agency can release it.
  • Searching is left to you or a title professional, even though the records are public.
  • Birth and death certificates come from the county health department, and divorce and marriage records come from the clerk of courts and probate court.

Let the title company run the lien search. Property tax liens are the treasurer's business, so raise those with that office.

Other documents the Recorder handles

Beyond deeds, the office records mortgages, mortgage releases, plats and financing statements under the Uniform Commercial Code that relate to real estate. Surveys are not usually filed there, so ask your lender or title company for one. If your home is in a subdivision, a plat map can be found by searching the subdivision name, and it shows lot lines and streets without any buildings.

Certified copies carry the office's stamp, so a printout from home cannot be certified. Come to the counter or request them by mail with a self-addressed stamped envelope. A document that cites an earlier recorded one through a marginal notation costs an extra charge per reference.

Searching records and guarding against deed fraud

The recorder's website offers a public records search and, as a trial, a newer mobile-friendly portal that opens recorded documents on a phone. Parcels can also be found on a GIS map kept by the county engineer, searchable by owner name, address or parcel number.

The site also offers Property Fraud Alert, a free service that monitors your name and flags new filings. It cannot block fraud, so treat it as an early warning. Notaries get a similar free service that watches for their name or commission number.

Scioto County homes in brief

Scioto County has an estimated 71,365 residents, 33,078 housing units and 28,864 households. Owners occupy 68.4 percent of homes, and the typical owner-occupied home is valued at $137,900. Median gross rent is $742. Portsmouth is the only city, with New Boston, Otway, Rarden and South Webster as villages. Much of the western half is forest, so acreage sales are common.

Property tax dates and your sale

State law splits the annual real estate bill into two installments, the later one falling on June 20 unless extended. The county moved the later installment in 2026 because of House Bill 186, so read the date printed on your bill. Your closing agent requests a tax payoff from the treasurer, whose office is at 602 7th Street, Room 102.

For assessment dates, appeals and relief programs, see the Scioto County property tax guide on this site.

On closing day the order is the same for a cash sale or a financed one: the notary witnesses your signature, the title company holds back the tax payoff, the auditor endorses the deed, and the recorder records it. If a lender is paid off, the release of mortgage is filed separately.

Ask the title company for a certified copy of the recorded deed once it is done. It carries the office's stamp and works for later loans or sales, and it is the only form of copy that counts as official.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

When can I visit the Scioto County Recorder?

Weekdays from 8:00 am, with the last service at 4:00 pm, in Room 110 at 602 7th St., Portsmouth. Call (740) 355-8304 to check.

How do I pay to record a deed in Scioto County?

Pay by cash or by a check made out to "Scioto County Recorder". Checks payable to anyone else are refused. The county has also adopted a $5.00 record preservation fee.

Is a notary required on a Scioto County deed?

Yes. Every transfer is signed before a notary. Ohio law also allows a judge, a clerk of court, the county auditor, the county engineer or a mayor to take the acknowledgment.

Does the recorder issue a new deed when I pay off my mortgage?

No. A new deed is issued only when the property is transferred. When the loan is satisfied, your lender files a release of mortgage as a separate recorded document.

Can the recorder tell me whether my title is clear?

No. The office is not allowed to give opinions on title. A professional title examiner or abstractor reviews the recorder's index along with records at other county offices.

Seneca County Recorder: location and role

The Seneca County Recorder works out of the county building at 109 S. Washington Street in Tiffin, the same building that houses the Auditor and the Treasurer. The Recorder's line is 419-447-4434. The office files deeds and mortgages in the order they arrive and marks each with the exact time of presentation, a duty found in ORC 317.13.

The county covers 553 square miles, nearly 80 percent of it farmland, and Tiffin sits on both banks of the Sandusky River. Fostoria and Bellevue each lie partly inside the county line, so expect a deed here to describe anything from a Tiffin bungalow to a few acres on a county road. Population has slipped from 61,901 in 1980 to 55,069 in 2020, and many sellers are heirs or owners of houses that need work. Whatever the condition, the sale ends the same way: a deed stamped at the Auditor and then filed with the Recorder.

Which office gets the deed first?

The Auditor does. Every transfer document has to be presented there before it can be recorded, under ORC 319.203. The Auditor sits in Suite 2206 of the same building, answers at 419-447-0692, and keeps weekday hours.

Bring and pay the following at the Auditor's counter:

  • A conveyance fee of $4.00 per thousand dollars conveyed.
  • A transfer fee of fifty cents for each parcel named in the deed.
  • A check made out to the Seneca County Auditor for the correct total. Blank checks are refused, and a wrong amount returns the paperwork unrecorded.
  • The state's DTE 100 form, or DTE 100 (EX) if the transfer qualifies for an exemption. Both are on the Auditor's forms page next to an online fee calculator.

The base figure comes from ORC 319.54(G)(3), which sets the state-level charge. Section 322.02 separately lets a board of county commissioners levy a transfer tax up to thirty cents per hundred. Seneca County uses one combined local rate, so ask the Auditor for the total when you budget for closing.

What a deed must contain

State law requires the grantor's signature to be acknowledged before an official such as a notary, judge, clerk of a court of record, county auditor, county engineer or mayor, as ORC 5301.01 lists them. That one rule covers deeds, mortgages, land contracts and leases.

Seneca County adds its own demands. The legal description must name the township or the city or village, the county and the state, and carry the right parcel numbers. The Tax Map Office reviews every description, and the wording should match the prior deed or the new survey exactly. The tax map line is 419-448-5719.

Splits are the slow part. A survey is generally needed, and the approving body depends on location: the Seneca Regional Planning Commission outside municipalities, the city engineer inside a city, village council inside a village. After January 1, 2027, splits, resurveys and combinations will appear in property tax records only from tax year 2028. Anyone selling a piece of a larger parcel should start the survey early.

What does recording a deed cost?

The Recorder's fee follows ORC 317.32. For a standard instrument the statute pairs a base fee with a housing trust fund fee, and it allows a county to add a preservation surcharge. Totals differ from county to county, so phone the Seneca County Recorder for the current amount. A short payment can bring the deed back.

Charges tied to a Seneca County deed
ChargeAmountPaid to
Conveyance fee$4.00 per thousand dollars conveyedCounty Auditor
Transfer fee$.50 per parcelCounty Auditor
First two pages recorded$17 base and $17 housing trust fundCounty Recorder
Each page after two$4 base and $4 housing trust fundCounty Recorder
Preservation surchargeUp to $5, if the county adopts itCounty Recorder

Searching and filing online

Ohio law now requires every recorder to offer electronic recording of real property conveyances and to publish electronic indexes and images for instruments recorded from January 1, 1980 forward, free of any access fee (ORC 317.13). Ask the Seneca County Recorder which e-recording vendor the office uses.

The Auditor's site is the easiest place to start a search. It reaches any parcel by name, address or map and shows the appraisal and payment history. It also publishes a real estate sales report, where sellers can read recent Seneca County sale prices. Five public computers are available in the building: two in the Auditor's office, two with the Treasurer and one at the Recorder.

From signing to a recorded deed

The order of steps rarely changes. The seller signs the deed in front of a notary. The deed and the DTE form go to the Auditor with a check for the conveyance and transfer fees, and the Auditor stamps it. Then the stamped deed goes next door to the Recorder with the recording fee. The Recorder times the filing, indexes it and returns the original.

A title company carries a deed through these steps at a closing. A family member handling a transfer alone can do the same in person, and all three offices are in the same Tiffin building. Before you go, confirm the total with the Auditor and the Recorder, and bring the prior deed so the legal description can be checked against it.

The Recorder can turn a deed away in two situations. ORC 317.13 lets the office refuse an instrument the Revised Code does not require or authorize to be recorded, or one the recorder reasonably believes is materially false or fraudulent. The filer can then ask the common pleas court for an order.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Seneca County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Property taxes and relief programs

The Auditor values the county's roughly 35,539 parcels and the Treasurer bills and collects. A closing agent asks the Treasurer for the payoff on any half still open, and a seller can look up the payment history on the Auditor's site first.

  • Value complaints go to a three-member Board of Revision. File between January 1 and March 31 with original notarized signatures.
  • A further appeal after the Board rules goes to the state Board of Tax Appeals or the local common pleas court within 30 days of the notice.
  • The homestead exemption for older or disabled owners is filed with the Auditor by December 31. For 2026 bills, new applicants needed $40,000 or less in Ohio adjusted gross household income, and disabled-veteran owners face no income test.

Ohio also has a veteran-related exemption created by House Bill 59 and codified at ORC 5709.17. Ask the Auditor whether a property qualifies before a sale closes.

Frequently asked questions

Do I record a Seneca County deed with the Auditor or the Recorder?

Both, in that order. The Auditor collects the conveyance fees and stamps the deed, then the Recorder files it.

What if my Seneca County deed has the wrong fee on the check?

The paperwork is sent back unrecorded. Incorrect fees and blank checks both cause rejection, so call 419-447-0692 for the amount before you write the check.

Can the Recorder turn down a deed?

Yes, in two situations. The recorder may refuse an instrument the Revised Code does not require or authorize to be recorded, or one believed to be materially false or fraudulent. The filer can ask the common pleas court for an order.

Is an attorney needed to transfer a house in Seneca County?

No law makes one mandatory. Still, the Tax Map Office checks every legal description and a mismatch holds up the sale, so many owners ask a title company or attorney to prepare the deed.

Until when can I contest a Seneca County valuation?

Through March 31 of the year after the tax year in question. Use the Board of Revision complaint form with notarized original signatures. The Auditor at 419-447-0692 can say which tax year applies to your parcel.

Where to take a deed in Shelby County

Take it to the Shelby County Recorder on the second floor of the county annex at 129 E. Court Street in Sidney. Phone 937-498-7270 or fax 937-498-7272 to reach staff. The counter takes new recordings a quarter hour before the staff stops other business. Monday to Thursday that means a 4:15 p.m. cutoff against a 4:30 p.m. close, and on Fridays 11:45 a.m. against noon. Plan to arrive well ahead of those times.

The Recorder keeps the county's real estate records, which reach back to the county's start, when the land was still part of Miami County. The online index covers July 1, 1989 forward. Older research means a trip to the office, and staff will help, though they do not do genealogy searches for outsiders.

Sidney is the only city in the county. The rest is villages, townships and farmland along the Great Miami River, so a deed here may describe a Sidney street lot, a village house or acreage. The county has 48,230 residents. A farmhouse on a few acres may need a survey or a split approved before it can be deeded separately, so ask the Auditor's office early about description rules.

What does Shelby County charge to record a deed?

Under the 2025 schedule, a deed costs $39 for its first two pages, with $8 for every added page. Most recording fees climbed $5 on January 1, 2025, after Senate Bill 94 added a document preservation surcharge, which ORC 317.32 limits to five dollars.

Shelby County Recorder charges, 2025 schedule
ServiceCharge
Deed, mortgage, lease and most filings$39 covers the first two pages
Each added page or attachment$8
Marginal notation$4 each
Non-standardization fee, per document$20
Plat, 11 by 17 inches$40
Plat, 24 by 36 inches$86
UCC financing statement$12 plus $4 per name indexed

Count the pages before you write the check, because the total moves with each added sheet and each attachment.

What recorder staff look for in a deed

The Recorder's rules are plain:

  • Every document needs a legal description, and it must read as it does on the prior deed. A description with missing parts is rejected.
  • Mail filings need a self-addressed stamped envelope. Without postage for the return, the office holds the document.
  • Marginal notations require the volume and page of the earlier record, and each one adds $4.
  • An affidavit has to say who the current owner of the property is.

The grantor's signature must be acknowledged by an authorized officer, usually a notary, under ORC 5301.01. An unacknowledged deed is not ready for the counter.

The county also posts a public notice on old deed language. Any clause that limits the sale, rental or use of a dwelling by race, color, sex, religion, national origin, handicap or familial status is invalid under federal fair housing law and cannot be enforced, even if it sits in a decades-old recorded deed.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Shelby County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Who collects the conveyance fee?

The Shelby County Auditor does, before the Recorder files anything. The real estate transfer fee is $4 per $1,000 of sale price plus $.50 per parcel.

The rate rests on ORC 319.54(G)(3) and the county option in ORC 322.02. The county option falls on the grantor, which makes the seller the usual payer when the deed is delivered.

A few transfers are exempt, among them family gifts, corrective deeds and deeds where no money changes hands. Ask the Auditor before assuming a deal qualifies.

From signing to a recorded deed

There are four steps, in this order. The grantor signs before a notary. The deed goes to the Shelby County Auditor with the transfer fee. The deed then goes to the Recorder, with the recording fee and a stamped return envelope if it travels by mail. Last, the Recorder indexes it, and the new owner's name appears in the county's records.

A title company normally carries a deed through those steps at a closing. A family member handling a transfer alone can do the same in person or by mail. Both offices are in Sidney, so ask each for its current hours before you go, and remember that the Recorder stops taking recordings 15 minutes before it closes.

Once the filing posts, the online index from July 1, 1989 forward lets anyone, including the seller, confirm the deed went on record.

Property tax records and relief programs

The Auditor's real estate section covers valuation and tax rates, revaluation information, owner occupancy and homestead tax reductions, delinquent payment plans and razed or damaged structures. A seller can search a parcel there to see the value on record before listing.

  • A value dispute begins as a Board of Revision complaint. ORC 5715.19 allows filing with the auditor until March 31 of the next year, or until the first-half collection closes if that falls later.
  • The 2026 homestead reduction for seniors and disabled owners is $29,700 of value, with the application filed in the same year by December 31.
  • Back taxes can sometimes be paid through a delinquent payment plan. Ask the Auditor for terms.

At closing the title agent requests the tax payoff from the county. Because Ohio bills real estate in two halves, the amount owed depends on when in the year the sale closes.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Shelby County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling a house that needs work

Many Shelby County houses are older village homes or farmhouses, and some need repairs a lender would balk at. A sale to a cash buyer is one route. The deed process described above is the same either way: signature before a notary, the Auditor's transfer fee, then the Recorder.

If the house came to you through a family estate, gather the recorded deed, any affidavit that names the current owner, and the death or probate paperwork your title company asks for. The Recorder will only file what is complete and acknowledged, so a missing signature or notary stamp costs you a second trip. For a mailed filing, add the stamped return envelope and a check for the exact fee. A cash buyer or title company usually handles these details, but it helps to know what they are doing on your behalf.

Before you sign a contract, check three things. Confirm the legal description on your current deed is complete, since a description with missing parts is rejected. Ask the Auditor whether the transfer qualifies for an exemption. And find out whether any back taxes need a payoff at closing, so the title agent is not surprised.

Frequently asked questions

What are the Shelby County Recorder's hours for recording a deed?

New recordings are accepted until 4:15 p.m. Monday to Thursday and until 11:45 a.m. Friday. Other office business continues 15 minutes longer each day.

How much is the Shelby County recording fee for a two-page deed?

It is $39 on the 2025 schedule, which covers the first two pages. Pages beyond that cost $8 each, a non-standard document adds $20, and each marginal notation adds $4.

Will the Recorder hold my deed if I mail it?

Yes, if you leave out the return envelope. Mailed documents need a stamped, self-addressed envelope, and without one the office holds the paper instead of mailing it back.

What is the Shelby County conveyance fee?

The real estate transfer fee is $4 per $1,000 of sale price plus fifty cents for each parcel. It is paid at the Auditor's office, ahead of recording.

Can I search Shelby County deeds from home?

Partly. The Recorder's website carries an index from July 1, 1989 forward. Earlier books stay at the office, where staff help visitors search but do not take genealogy requests.
